# llmx - Development Status

## A routing row with no candidate, on both backends (2026-10-25, branch fix/route-oob on main 07facf1b6, C2DEV's DECISIONs of 2026-10-24 10:40 and 2026-10-25 00:12, amendment 4, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **The bug:** a row whose softmax is not finite (a NaN or infinite score, or every score -inf) has NaN probabilities, of which no pick is ever taken; the device then picked the invalid id, marked it at `prob[0xffffffff]` outside its shared table and gave each pick a weight of one k-th, while the CPU picked expert 0 again and again; `moe_group` counted the invalid id at `hist[0xffffffff]`, and the routed row kernels read the rows of expert 0xffffffff.
- **The contract (backend.hpp):** such a row has no candidate, its k ids are `Backend::kNoExpert` with weights 0, and the routed products leave an entry without an expert unwritten and add nothing for it.
- **The fix:** `route_experts` on the CPU gives a row whose sum is NaN `kNoExpert` picks, and its grouping and weighted sum pass them over; on the device `moe_route` marks nothing for an invalid pick and weights it 0, `moe_group` counts it in no tile, the routed row kernels (`matmul_row.comp`, `matmul_vec_q8.comp`) return for it before reading a row, and `moe_combine` skips its slot, reading the ids beside the weights.
- **Test:** `backend-vulkan`, on the CPU and the device, routes a row of NaN scores, a row with one NaN among finite scores and a row with one finite score and the rest -inf, and runs the routed gate-up and down calls on two decode rows and on a 70-row prompt at extent 512 with every second row without candidates; it fails on main on the CPU's ids and passes with the fix on the Radeon VII; `backend-group` holds the CPU's half on the hosted runners.
- **Gates:** to run before landing: byte identity against main on a device for the tiny qwen3moe, qwen35moe and Flash fixtures and a routed real model on an MI50, CTest and the CPU suite, the Radeon VII device tests, and the hosted run.
## A model bench's ids span the vocabulary (2026-10-25, branch feat/bench-ids on main 07facf1b6, the coordinator's order of 2026-10-25, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **The bug:** `bench --model` drew every id below 1000, so on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next its prompts read a few cached rows of the 26.8 GiB per-layer table, where a text reads a distinct row a token from the file.
  On four MI50s its pp2048 on 2x2 read 726 tok/s against 130-175 tok/s for served wiki prompts of 4k-16k tokens through the same build (2026-10-24 comparison against the gfx906 HIP fork, test machine `castagna/run/out1` and `out2`).
- **The fix:** the ids come from one function, `bench_ids`, which spreads a fixed seed's ids over the whole vocabulary by a multiply-shift of the generator's 32 bits, as a text's ids spread; the prompt, the depth's history and the decode tokens keep their own seeds.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on main: `cli-output` holds `bench_ids` to spanning a 151936- and a 248320-token vocabulary (the largest of 4096 past nine tenths, 3900 distinct at least) and to staying inside it, a 16-token vocabulary included.
- **Measured** (test machine, GPU 9, CPUs 14-15, ABBA, pp512 and tg64 with 3 counted runs; main 07facf1b6 against the branch, each built clean): ordinary models are unchanged, Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 pp 8961.0 against 8951.5 and tg 410.8 against 412.4 tok/s, Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M pp 786.9 against 786.6 and tg 82.8 against 82.6.
- **A new series:** on a routed model the ids decide the experts, and on a table-reading model the rows read, so `bench --model` figures of routed models (Qwen3-30B-A3B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Flash and the like) and of table-reading models (Flash's per-layer table) start a new series at this commit and are not comparable with figures taken before it; dense models without a table are unchanged beyond noise (C2DEV's review of 2026-10-25 02:17).
- **Left:** Flash's bench figure before and after on six cards, queued behind DDEV's runs; the hosted run.

## A Vulkan table past 4 GiB gathered through views of whole rows (2026-10-25, branch feat/lookup-wide on main 07facf1b6, the coordinator's order of 2026-10-25, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **The bug:** `embed` and `embed_ids` bound a table once and indexed it with 32-bit byte offsets, so a resident table past 4 GiB, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's 26.8 GiB per-layer table with `--lookup-storage device`, gave other rows than its own past 2^32 bytes and a binding past the device's storage-buffer range.
- **The fix:** the gather takes the table as views of whole rows (`table_views`), each within one binding's range and 32-bit byte indices and beginning on the storage-buffer offset alignment with its first row a skew in, and records one dispatch a view (`gather_views`); `shaders/embed.comp` reads rows lo to hi of its view at the skew and leaves other rows to the other views, the last view writing the zero rows of device ids past the table.
  A table that fits one binding is one view and one dispatch, as before.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on main: `vulkan-buffer` holds the views of Flash's table (320001536 IQ4_NL rows of 90 bytes) and four other tables to one binding's range, the alignment and every row once; main's single binding fails four of its six cases.
  With the fix, `backend-vulkan` reads F32, Q8_0 and IQ4_NL tables past 4 GiB through `embed` and `embed_ids` bit for bit against the CPU; with main's gather the same check fails (`a F32 table past 4 GiB gives other rows than the CPU`, MI50).
- **Measured** (test machine, GPU 8, CPUs 2-5; branch and main 07facf1b6 each built clean from their own commit):
  - A synthetic Qwen4Exp file, the tiny reference fixture with its per-layer table grown to 617401564 F32 rows (4.9 GB) and large hash multipliers, gives the same 28 logits rows with the table on the device and read from its file; main with the table on the device differs in all 28.
  - Byte identity against main on the device for Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M (16 logits rows of a 21-token prompt).
  - Timing, Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, ABBA twice, pp512 and tg128 with 5 counted runs: main 8746.4 and 402.8 tok/s, the branch 8747.5 and 402.7.
  - Radeon VII under the AMD proprietary driver 26.5.2: `vulkan-buffer` and `backend-vulkan` pass, the tables past 4 GiB included.
  - The numerics fingerprint changes with the shader, so the disk cache proves files of earlier builds at their first use, as for any kernel change.
- **Reach on Flash:** a resident table sits whole on each device that runs its layer, so four 32 GB MI50s refuse it in two tensor groups (51.56 GiB needed on the first group's devices) and in a layer split (51.14 GiB); six in a layer split fit it beside layer 1 alone.
- **Left:** the six-card real-text proof (served 4k, 8k and 16k wiki prompts and the 20 served prompts, the table on the devices against read from its file, greedy texts identical), which waits for GPUs 4-9; the suite on a device; the hosted run; C2DEV's review.

## A prompt in consecutive passes at consecutive stages (2026-10-23, branch feat/prompt-pipeline on main 07facf1b6, MULTI-DEVICE phase 4, DDEV's DESIGN of 15:16, F2DEV's DECISION of 15:18, C2DEV's review of 2026-10-25 00:12 and the coordinator's revision of F2DEV's first amendment, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Goal:** on a pipelined split a prompt's slices run on several stages at once, so prompt reading at depth stops taking the stages in turn (main's lone 8k tail at 100k depth had one stage busy 0.84 to 0.89 of the time), faster than main in every cell of the leg, the reply leads kept.
- **The change:**
  - Runtime: `Sequence::flights_` counts a sequence's passes. `begin_pass` takes a sequence in flight alone in its pass once each of its passes holds it alone, has committed the first stage and does not want its logits, and it holds no mark. `at_stage` checks at each stage, before any work, that the pass meets the history it continues. `abort_pass` rolls a sequence's later passes back first and returns their slots.
  - Scheduler: `continues` lets a prompt or a read-ahead job in flight take a free slot alone after a slice formed in an earlier round, never while a request could not grow or for a cancelled request, leaving a slot free beside generated rows, and no job while a request waits for its seat or room; `recall` abandons a continuing job's passes so it gives way at once.
    `holders` counts a request by its earliest pass. `fail_pass` and `abort_all` abandon a continued prompt's later slices, and a round passes over the slots a failure emptied during its steps; a deferred host stage stays with the pass formed before the round's formation. `/v1/health` counts the passes so formed (`passes.since_start.continued`).
- **Done:** the runtime rules with `placement` (two, three and four stages against `prefill`, the refusals, abandoning and a failure at the last stage) and `arch-qwen35` (the hybrid split, a checkpoint at 128); the scheduler with `server-passes-cpu` (lone and beside a reply, two and three stages, P = S and S + 1, with and without the rule) and `cache-scenario`; `server-passes`' simulated round restated with continued prompts and their invariant, 60000 schedules passing; docs. A continuing job over a two-CPU split with two passes in flight reads its rows as alone (`server-resume`), leg B of `cache-scenario` on the split gives way while its job continues, a lone prompt's slice failing at the last stage with a later slice in flight ends the request and frees the pool (`server-passes-cpu`), and a stage the scheduler records inline quiets its stages' threads before the pass is undone (`run_pass_stage`'s `before_undo`).
- **Gates (at 40c742405, before C2DEV's amendments):** the build, CTest (81 of 81), the CPU suite and the simulated round (2000 schedules) on Linux; served byte identity against main 55a115a05, a 6000-character prompt and 64 greedy tokens with log-probabilities, of Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M on one CPU and on a layer split over two MI50s, where each prompt continued in 20 passes, all identical; the Flash 2x2 identity of the device leg identical.
- **Gates at the landing head:** the build, CTest (81 of 81), the CPU suite and the simulated round (2000 schedules) on Linux, CTest (82 of 82) on Windows; the hosted run.
- **The lone-prompt leg (2026-10-25, `runs/p4leg2`):** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL at production's flags, untraced, main 07facf1b6's src (55a115a05 for the runtime), phase 4 and phase 4 without the slice gate, in the order main, p4, p4ng, p4ng, p4, main on each placement, GPUs 4-7 with GPUs 8-9 idle; tok/s, the first main run on 2x2 in the slow machine state of 2026-10-24 (its other cells run at the second's pace).

  | Placement, arm | 100k prefix | 8k tail at 100k, alone | Reply alone | Tail beside a reply | Reply beside the tail |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 2x2, P = 2, main | 141.2, 312.0 | 124.7, 201.4 | 40.57, 59.43 | 88.5, 126.5 | 3.44, 3.59 |
  | 2x2, P = 2, phase 4 | 535.1, 530.7 | 324.5, 323.1 | 59.90, 59.94 | 126.3, 126.4 | 3.61, 3.58 |
  | 2x2, P = 2, without the slice gate | 531.6, 531.7 | 323.4, 323.6 | 59.48, 60.27 | 126.5, 126.5 | 3.58, 3.60 |
  | layer over 4, P = 4, main | 305.0, 302.5 | 192.7, 196.9 | 53.61, 54.13 | 113.0, 105.6 | 9.71, 7.12 |
  | layer over 4, P = 4, phase 4 | 919.6, 917.4 | 536.5, 532.4 | 55.12, 55.25 | 181.4, 180.0 | 12.55, 12.36 |
  | layer over 4, P = 4, without the slice gate | 913.8, 915.1 | 529.8, 534.2 | 55.67, 55.17 | 157.3, 161.0 | 9.12, 9.82 |

  Phase 4 reads the prefix 1.7 and 3.0 times as fast as main and the tail alone 1.6 and 2.7 times, the reply alone level; beside a reply the layer split's tail and reply both gain, and the slice gate is level alone and ahead beside a reply on the layer split (181 against 157 to 161 tok/s, 12.4 to 12.6 against 9.1 to 9.8), so it stays.
- **Open after landing (recorded, not waived):** the 3x2 and P = S + 1 cells; the reference's prompt rates beside each cell.
- **Measured, interleaved (devlog RESULT 2026-10-24 12:06):** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL on 2x2 at production's flags, untraced, base b9bc503dd against ec38648b5, 14 runs ABBA.
  Every cell moved between two machine states, which follow other work on GPUs 8-9 (on stage 1's root complex) and the host; in the fast state both arms give 1 reply about 58 tok/s, the 20k handover prompt 311 to 335 and the replies after it 30 to 31, in the slow state about half.
  The one fast pair in a row is level: 1 reply 57.7 against 58.3, handover prompt 312.2 against 312.6, the reply during it 3.15 against 3.31 and after it 31.02 against 31.12 (phase 4 first). No pass continued during any handover, since a reply in flight keeps its slot.
- **The first device leg (devlog FINDING 2026-10-24 07:26):** traced builds, each base cell 15 to 20 minutes before its phase 4 cell while other CPU and GPU work came and went, so its reply figures do not compare; a lone 8k tail at 100k depth read 107.4 against 148.8 new tok/s on 2x2 and 120.9 against 533.8 on the layer split, the 2x2 gain coming from the base's 2.1 s of host time between slices moving under the next stage and not from stages overlapping.
- **Gotchas:** a request alone of several slices now has passes in flight together, so its stages are recorded on their threads (`recorded_apart`); a continued slice and the slices before it hold their request alone, so a failure takes only that request's slices, where an earlier slice shared with a decoder made `fail_pass` abandon the decoder's row too (`server-passes` schedule 5).
  A continuation that takes the last free slot leaves a reply that retires meanwhile waiting for a slice at the last stage, and a job that always continues never leaves flight to give way (`cache-scenario` leg B); the rule's conditions and `recall` are what prevent each.
  A cancelled, or a growth plan's, request that kept continuing would never leave flight, and a failure that takes other slices empties slots the round's steps still name; the simulation found each (schedules 9, 505, 91 and 2133).
  `serve --device cpu,cpu` is refused, so a CPU split is checked through the tests, not a served identity.

## A twin left on values a norm or SiLU changed (2026-10-24, branch fix/stale-twin on main 55a115a05, found by DDEV's fused-kernel DESIGN of 13:15, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **The bug:** the Vulkan backend's `rms_norm_rows` and `silu_mul` are exempt from the dispatch's clear of the cached activation twin (`XqTag`) and set the tag only when they write a twin, so a call that writes none (`n % 32 != 0`, or a norm over part of each row with another stride) left the old twin tagged on a buffer whose values it changed, and a matmul reading that buffer read the old twin.
- **The fix:** such a call drops the tag where its output overlaps the twin's source (`overlaps_twin`), as the matmuls already do.
- **Test:** `backend-vulkan` writes a twin with a norm and with a SiLU over two rows, writes over part of each in place without one, and holds the matmul from the written buffer to the same matmul from a fresh copy of its values, under f16 and int8; it fails on main (the norm case) on the Radeon VII and passes with the fix.
- **Reach:** no model calls either kernel that way today (Qwen3's head norms go through `norm_rope_kv`, the qwen35 and Flash ones through `norm_rope_partial`, and every width is a multiple of 32), so no model output changes; the fix keeps the backend's contract for the next caller.
- **Gates (at 69b26eef3 on 3acbf483f, the code rebased unchanged):** byte identity against main on the CPU and the Radeon VII for Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 and Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M (16 logits rows of a 927- and 955-token prompt and 64 greedy tokens each, identical but for the timing lines); the 13 Vulkan CTests on the Radeon VII; CTest 81 of 81 on Windows; the CPU suite on Linux and the hosted run at the landing head.

## TQ1_0 / TQ2_0 CPU and Vulkan support (2026-10-25)

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Read-only TQ1_0 and TQ2_0 model weights | Done on CPU and Vulkan. No quantize writer. |

The paired decoders live in the quant owner and the existing Vulkan product owners. Model, loader, CLI and server paths consume the shared type registry without format-specific dispatch. Both formats cover dense, tied and routed matrices, embedding, grouped products, split placement and wider dtype fallback. Native FP4 acceleration is unrelated; NVFP4 is the next quant family.

- **Correctness:** independent packed-block oracles, CPU and Radeon VII checks, frozen tiny HF calibration and ordinary MI50 checks pass. CPU tensor widths 2/4, Vulkan TP2 and layer-split tiny checks pass. Released short rankings/NLL and raw/chat 16K F32 checks pass. CPU default depth passes; Vulkan default raw passes. The two frozen Vulkan chat captures each retain 506 exact / 5 accepted ties / 1 miss. BOSS approved the one-position existing-main exception on 2026-10-25 after clean main with exact decoded weights reproduced it. All 512 positions were reclassified with unchanged `tests/common.py`; each has one separately reported baseline exception and zero unapproved misses. The general 0.1 rule, other bounds and original failures remain. [Approval and retained-capture results](benchmarks/tq-approved-existing-main-20261025.json), [policy](PRECISION.md#independent-hf-depth-acceptance-agreed-2026-10-01).
- **Performance:** the final clean MI50 comparison uses llmx `a0fa25492` and mx Vulkan `c4d12e2c` in the same image, default clocks/power, four interleaved pairs per cell, with all samples and activity retained. TQ1 prefill improves 93.30% to 139.26%, decode 45.12% to 45.43%. TQ2 prefill improves 81.02% to 105.74%, while decode is -0.31% and +0.22%, with mixed-sign paired differences. Those minor decode differences do not establish a regression, and the substantial prefill gains satisfy the first-stage workload tradeoff. Existing Q8 main comparisons are within 0.38% in both phases, and existing-format CPU/Vulkan identity passes. These are independent PP/TG phases, not request latency. [All final pairs and activity flags](benchmarks/tq-final-clean-mx-20261024.json). Matching mx ROCm remains the later all-quant tuning phase.
- **Hosted coverage:** run [40125669040](https://github.com/mxxm-t/llmx/actions/runs/40125669040) passed native tests (68 Ubuntu/UBSan/macOS, 69 Windows, 81 Vulkan) and TSan; the six Python failures were only the stale CLI unsupported-TQ fixture. The corrected Q8_1 negative fixture passed all five configurations in [40128390450](https://github.com/mxxm-t/llmx/actions/runs/40128390450). Previously skipped HF F32-cache, CPU split, server-mix and Windows plain executable coverage completed in [40128953473](https://github.com/mxxm-t/llmx/actions/runs/40128953473). Its temporary-workflow static failures were covered by restored-tree run [40130076545](https://github.com/mxxm-t/llmx/actions/runs/40130076545). Original red runs stay red. Root verified their logs and the source deltas; the temporary workflows do not land. [Final source and coverage audit](benchmarks/tq-landing-source-audit-20261025.json).
- **Landing and review:** lands as one squashed fast-forward from main `eaea90857`. Runtime/build inputs remain those tested at `a0fa25492`; the only intervening test change is the separately qualified `tests/cli.py` negative fixture. Approval and final support documentation change no executable behavior. All 134 project Markdown pages were reconciled against the prior review, with the support, precision and status pages updated for completion and dated diagnostic records retained below. Final docs/dead-code checks apply to the tree that lands. No production restart or configuration change is part of this feature.
- **Limits:** read-only storage support is not a recommendation for the released fixtures' model quality. Their very poor perplexity and all original diagnostic failures remain recorded. The scoped exception applies only to the pinned files and frozen captures; later files, changes and failures cannot inherit it automatically. No global tolerance or reference selection changes.

## A history's own drafts rest by their match's length, and a pass reserves the draft rows its cap allows (2026-10-24, branch feat/draft-depth on main 5ab233d32, F2DEV's DECISIONs of 2026-10-23 11:20 and 11:24 and the coordinator's rule of 2026-10-24, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** the owner asked for longer drafts on long lookup matches. The measurement of 2026-10-23 (Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0, the match profile's 30 prompts, greedy, 400 tokens, one MI50; kept shares from the replies' ids; /zpool1/llmx-ldev-scratch/depth27/analysis) found a match of 32 tokens or more keeping its 16th draft 0.82 of the time and one of 8 to 11 0.25, so one acceptance for every match let short matches' misses rest and price long ones.
- **What lands:**
  - `spec::Record` keeps the history's own drafts in three acceptances by the match's length at the draft's start (`match_bucket`: 8 to 15, 16 to 31, 32 or more), the length found by extending the eight-token occurrence backwards in `Lookup::convincing`'s own walk, at most 32; `lookup_first` rests a draft on its bucket, `verified` records into it, the server's `tally_` keeps the same buckets as each one's prior, and `tally` sums them for the figures.
  - The draft rows a pass reserves are `min(kDraftRows, max_seqs x draft_max)` (`Scheduler::draft_rows`), where they were 64 whatever the cap: 3 for one request at 3, 48 for 16 at 3, 64 from 4 drafts a request for 16 up.
  - `--draft-max`'s default stays 3, by the coordinator's rule: 15 only if neither model had a kind slower than at 3 beyond the rounds' spread.
- **Measured and not landed:** `generate` and `chat` priced as the server (`draft_depths` over their own measured steps, verifies and chains), and depths only at the plateau ends of the decode builds (`Backend::decode_plateau_end`); with a default of 3 neither has a measured use; both, built and gated, are kept on gitea exp/draft-depth-priced at c187f74fe.
- **The gates** (two rounds the second reversed, the 30 prompts greedy at 400 tokens, one at a time through a server's streamed route, decode tokens a second after the first token, the rounds' mean; /zpool1/llmx-ldev-scratch/gate-depth; every arm the ids of drafts off):
  - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, production's placement (2 stages x tensor width 2 on four MI50s, int8, `--drafter lookup,<MTP head Q4_K_M>`), `/v1/chat`, before the plateau pricing: off 29.5, cap 3 47.4, 7 47.4, 15 50.0, 31 48.1 over all kinds; code edits 82.9 at 3 and 132.8 at 15 (+60 percent), no chat kind slower at 15 beyond the spread, code questions 10 percent slower at 7 and 31.
  - Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 on one MI50, `serve --max-seqs 4`, `/v1/generate`, `lookup,embedded`: before the plateau pricing code edits 61.0 at 3 and 75.6 at 15 with the chat kinds 7 to 16 percent slower at 15, the server taking depth 2 on most verifies past a cap of 3; with it, code edits 60.4 against 75.2 (+24.6 percent) and code questions -9.1, document quotes -4.8, free chat -5.0, summaries -4.3 and structured -0.5 percent at 15 against 3, each beyond its rounds' spread (0.15 to 2.15). Hence the default stays 3.
  - Kept shares by position on the 27B from priced `generate --verbose` at 31: the MTP chain 2997/3464, 1875/2545, 666/886, 455/598 at positions 1 to 4, 147/213 at 8, 8/67 at 16; the history's own drafts 221/243 at 1, 105/137 at 8, 66/98 at 16, 49/88 at 31.
  - The fit: Flash's KV pool 655616 tokens at 3, 649728 at 15 and 644096 at 31 (1003584 without a drafter); the 27B's 22400 at 3, 20800 at 15, 19520 at 31 (29824 without), the difference the marks' rows, `--draft-max` + 1 a mark. Logits rows a pass under the old reserve `max_seqs + 64` at every cap, under the new `max_seqs + min(64, max_seqs x draft_max)`: Flash's 16 requests 64 at 3 against 80, the 27B's 4 requests 16 at 3 against 68.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on main: eleven missed eight-token matches rested the drafts of a match of 32 tokens. With the change, `spec`'s keyed record cases and its rounds at 7, 15 and 31 drafts, and `server-passes-cpu`'s reserve at 3, 31 and 63; CTest `spec`, `server-spec` and `server-passes-cpu` pass on Windows, docs and dead-code too.
- **A flaky case fixed beside it:** `server-resume-cache`'s trim case after a whole write failed once on the hosted Windows runner (run 40070872377): the job's read of the file outlasted the wait its prompt rate gives, so the job read its 512 rows itself and the read landed as a third donor (12 blocks against 8). On Linux the read takes 2 ms and the job forks it. The case now waits up to 60 s for the read (`DiskOptions::read_wait`), as the other disk cases do; the draft rows play no part, since the case's scheduler drafts nothing.
- **Left:** the hosted run, C2DEV's review. A deeper default waits on what makes the 27B's chat kinds keep their speed past a cap of 3, which neither the plateau pricing nor `generate`'s pricing did.

## IQ1_S / IQ1_M read-only support (completed; 2026-10-24)

Read-only CPU and Vulkan inference is qualified through the existing quant, embedding and matrix owners. Independent format/operator checks, tiny and released-file HF, CPU/Vulkan raw/chat 16K, layer/tensor split, HTTP integration and matched timing evidence are complete. No writer is added.

## Lookup rows read ahead (2026-10-23, branch feat/lookup-prefetch on feat/split-pacing b9bc503dd, item P of the Flash decode design of 2026-10-20 08:29, ranked first for cold text by F2DEV on 2026-10-23 11:14, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Goal:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's per-layer embedding rows, read from the table's file (`--lookup-storage file`), stop holding a decode token and a prompt.
  The probe of 2026-10-20 measured cold rows read one after another at 10.0 and 8.4 ms a decode token, against 3.8 and 3.3 ms with a token's 16 rows read at once on threads beside layer 0. A prompt read 7.4 and 8.1 ms a prompt token one row at a time, against 3.2 and 3.0 ms on 64 threads.
  Text a reply repeats, as TG256's, finds its rows in the page cache and gains nothing.
- **The change:** `WeightRows::start` deals a file read's runs to the table's `kReadThreads` (16) readers and returns at once, and `finish` takes the rows; there is no read of both in one call, the stage calling them apart.
  `Model::start_lookup` starts a stage's lookups as it begins, and `finish_lookup` takes each just before its layer, so the layers before it record and run meanwhile. No flag.
- **Done:** the reader and the runtime's two calls, the fit counting the table's read windows once; a read counts as started only once it is under way (F2DEV's review of 16:06); `weight-rows` checks a read started ahead, `finish` without a start, a start over an abandoned read, a start failing at an allocation after its checks leaving `finish` refusing, a scratch dropped mid-read, more runs than readers and a short file at `finish`; docs.
- **Measured on production's cell (2026-10-23, pleg):**
  - Setup: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL on 2x2 at production's flags (int8, f16 KV, `--lookup-storage file`, lookup and MTP drafting), GPUs 4-7, CPUs 6-13. Main 19a312f60 (build 6acd61ad) against P at 9f9a4c170, the reading code this head carries (build 13565a31), both git archives built the same way. Four servers in ABBA order, each fed 6 slices of about 500 tokens never fed before, with 256 greedy tokens each.

  | Arm | Decode, median of 12 slices | Time to first token, median | Decode per server (median) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | main | 33.34 tok/s | 5.01 s | 30.8, 34.3 |
  | P | 35.56 tok/s (+6.7%) | 5.13 s | 35.7, 33.8 |

  - A slice fed again to each server gave the same text on both arms.
  - Why it is a third of the probe's 15 to 25 percent: production on GPUs 0-3 reads the same file through the same page cache, so many of the slices' rows were already cached rather than cold; and LDEV's `llmx-ldev-gate-27b` ran on CPUs 10-11, inside the arms' CPUs, for the whole leg.
  - The warm-cache figure is the one that stands for production, which shares that page cache (the coordinator, 2026-10-23).
- **Gates:** the tests commit fails to build on main, which has no `start`, `finish` or `staging_bytes`, and its failed-start check fails on 2cf5a995d and passes here. CTest and the CPU suite passed at 9f9a4c170, docs and dead-code with them, but the placement case whose expectation this head changed, which passes here. Hosted run on github gate/train2-1023.
- **Gotchas:** the readers are the table's, one set of 15 threads a table (F2DEV's review of 15:25), so a table reads for one scratch at a time; a direct-read table holds a granule window for each of its 16 readers, which the fit counts once for the table (`WeightRows::staging_bytes`), and a buffered one none, its reads landing in the rows.

## Replies beside a prompt on a pipelined split (2026-10-23, branch feat/split-pacing on main eaa08d839, the interleaved rule, F2DEV's reviews of 2026-10-22 07:41 and 16:18 and the coordinator's approval, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Why:** on production's placement (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL, two stages of two MI50s, int8, lookup and MTP drafting) a reply beside an 8017-token prompt at 100k tokens of history got 0.33 to 1.03 tok/s against 58 alone. It rode the prompt's pass, which then wanted logits and held both requests through both stages one after the other, so a token came every 2 x 1.48 s; `--passes 3` changed nothing (devlog FINDING 2026-10-22 07:35).
- **The change:** `Pacing::interleaved`, the default where the placement is a pipelined split (`PlacedModel::pipelined_split`, beside `unpaced`).
  While replies and prompts both wait, generated rows go in passes of their own formed first, and each prompt slice goes in a pass of its own that wants no logits, cut by each device stage's `PieceSearch` with the whole slice's stage time as its piece and timed by the stage's recorder.
  A prompt's next slice is formed only once its last has retired at the first stage (`Request::slice_ticket_`), so a reply's pass formed meanwhile goes before it there.
  Outside an overlap every pass is formed as without pacing. `/v1/health` counts the passes of generated rows and the slices formed in an overlap.
- **Tests:** `server-passes` (the mode); `server-passes-cpu` on splits of two and three slow CPU devices at P = S and S + 1:
  - requests in turn form no interleaved pass;
  - a reply beside two prompts gets passes of its own, and no pass mixes a reply's rows with a prompt's slice or holds two prompts' slices;
  - a reply beside one prompt: once the prompt is sampled the rule forms no more passes, its request is in one of the next P passes, and each pass then holds one of the two decoders;
  - every reply is its reply alone.
- **Measured, the 100k cell:** GPUs 4 to 9; the 8017-token tail at 100195 tokens of depth beside a 600-token reply; tok/s; the prompt kept is its rate beside the reply over its rate alone in the same run.

  | Placement | Reply beside, main | Reply beside, rule | Longest gap, main | Longest gap, rule | Prompt kept, main | Prompt kept, rule |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 2x2, P = 2 | 0.72, 0.81 | 3.67, 3.82 | 4180, 3545 ms | 876, 818 ms | 0.91, 0.93 | 0.61 to 0.66 |
  | 2x2, P = 3 | - | 3.75 | - | 818 ms | - | 0.64 |
  | 3x2, P = 3 | 1.12 | 5.24, 6.05, 6.57 | 2860 ms | 578 to 931 ms | 1.08 | 0.68 to 0.82 |
  | 3x2, P = 4 | - | 6.35 | - | 499 ms | - | 0.74 |
  | layer over 4, P = 4 | - | 7.12 | - | 516 ms | - | 0.53 |

  The trade favours replies, the owner's standing choice for pacing: the prompt beside a reply keeps about two thirds of its rate, against about all of it before, for 4 to 6 times the reply's rate.
  Runs on this shared machine vary by up to 25 percent in phases that run the same code in both arms.
- **The handover (20255-token prompt beside a reply, then both decoding, 2x2):** prompt 305.9 tok/s; the reply 3.33 tok/s during it (longest gap 553 ms) and 30.66 after; the new reply 31.48 tok/s; two passes in flight 96 percent of the time after.
- **Probe (c), the `slice_ticket_` gate, kept:** without it, on the 20k handover, the prompt read at 295.1 against 261.0 tok/s and the reply got 3.40 against 4.25 tok/s, with the same longest gap and the same busy shares. Either way the stages did not overlap more, since the next slice still waits for the last stage.
- **Option (a), no drafts beside a prompt, dropped:**
  - As a switch: at 100k the reply fell to 2.46 (2x2) and 2.72 (3x2) tok/s against 3.67 and 6.57, and the prompt was level (121.6 against 125.3, 134.6 against 134.8 tok/s).
  - Through the pass price (the verifies' retracts priced, and overlap passes priced apart), against the head in the same session:
    - 100k: 2.84 and 2.75 tok/s against 3.82 and 6.05;
    - the 20k handover: 2.09 against 3.33 tok/s, and a prompt of 245.6 against 305.9;
    - decode-only at 2 and 4 replies: 53.8 and 80.6 against 67.2 and 122.1 tok/s, since the retracts were priced there too.
  - The patch is kept outside the tree.
- **Stage alternation, a limit on main:** a lone prompt at depth runs one stage at a time on main too.
  - Share of the tail window with that many stages busy, main: 2x2 one 0.89 and two 0.03; 3x2 one 0.84 and two or more 0.11.
  - The rule's 2x2 and 3x2 runs: two stages 0.18. A layer split over four single cards: two stages 0.28.
  - Why: a sequence is in one pass at a time, and a pass ends when its last stage is recorded, which waits for the stage before it. A tensor group's stage records with every sum waited for, so its recording lasts as long as its compute.
  - Inside a grouped stage's slice the card waits at sums 0.00 to 0.03 of the window and between slices 0.40 to 0.65 (the H4b figure). The repair is a sequence in consecutive passes at consecutive stages (MULTI-DEVICE phase 4), not cheaper sums.
- **Decode-only (1, 2 and 4 replies of 256 tokens):**
  - 2x2: 60.0, 39.8 + 34.0, 4 x 31.6 tok/s; two passes in flight 92 percent of the time.
  - 3x2: 54.0, 36.7 + 31.1, 4 x 25.2.
  - layer over 4: 50.8, 39.2 + 32.1, 4 x 32.3.
  - A stage's time at two replies on 2x2: compute 0.67 to 0.73, sum gaps 0.15 to 0.17, gaps between passes 0.11 to 0.16.
- **Against the reference's ROCm server (same cards, file and workload):** its FEATURES.md environment and `GGML_CUDA_CUBLAS_COMPUTE_TYPE=f32`, without which its hipBLAS GEMM of the file's 24 BF16 tensors fails on gfx906 (`CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR` at a 13-token prompt). It logged pipeline parallelism enabled. MTP was off, since it gave 13.4 tok/s alone against 29.8 without. Prompt cache was off (`-cram 0`); its slot checkpoints kept the 100k prefix.

  | 2x2 tail beside / alone | 123.4 / 201.8 tok/s | 302.4 / 301.3 tok/s |

## A reply is read again beside it, and a finished donor keeps what its next turn shares (2026-10-20, branch feat/reply-reread, rebased on main 19a312f60 on 2026-10-23, XDEV's REVIEW of 08:26 and F2DEV's DECISION of 08:29, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why (the FINDING of 06:39):** on production a cut conversation's long reply with reasoning was not read again while it was written: beside continuous replies the background allowance gave a job's step, which costs more than the allowance at depth, nothing (no credit beside replies, by rule), so the job's ids stood unread at the reply's end, another conversation's prompt came first, and the next turn read the reply again; and the reply's reasoning, which the next render leaves out, kept its rows on the devices and went to host memory and disk.
- **The change:** `BackgroundGrant` goes with its allowance, interval, credit and debt rules, `job_grant`, `job_rides`, `demand_beside`, `Pacing::refused`, the background figures of `/v1/health` (`pacing.background`) and the write budget (`write_left_`, `grant_writes`).
  A job's rows are the lowest-priority prompt rows under the one pacing: none while a request reads its prompt, the whole leftover budget while nothing generates either, and beside replies one piece after `kBackgroundGaps` (3) completed reply-only service gaps of a stage, a frequency in gaps and not a share of time; under the automatic rule the job is then the overlap's prompt, fed in pieces through the same search, and its every piece boundary serves three services before its next (`serve_gaps`); the round counts the passes of generated rows alone since a job's last pass (`reply_gaps_`).
  A turn-end write's segment is the blocks `kPieceMs` copies at `copy_block_ms_`, the copy's wait included, one block before any is measured: beside prompts alone a segment a round, beside replies only at background work's turn, after `kBackgroundGaps` (renamed from `kBackgroundShare`, a count of gaps) reply-only gaps from the same `reply_gaps_` the jobs count, the job and the write in turn when both wait (`Scheduler::write_turn`, `Cache::WriteTurn`, F2DEV's REVIEW of 2026-10-22 16:28), whole while nothing runs or waits, and the donor a request waits for first and whole. With the budget gone no donor is given nothing, which b95ae86e3 on main had to pass over. Each write begun counts as the move `write_started`.
  Once a finished request's next turn is given whole (`Scheduler::follow`), its donor keeps only the whole blocks the ids share with it (`Cache::trim`, `Donor::keep`): a dense model's donor is retracted there, or dropped where nothing is shared; a state model's stays whole on the devices, ending at its checkpoint, and is copied and written only to the prefix; paused donors, jobs' donors and raw continuations are kept whole.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on 53a7e81e2 and again rebased on main 6db4d22bd (Linux, the next turn reusing 512 of 768): `cache-scenario`'s production case of 2026-10-20 (a cut conversation's 512-token reply, half reasoning, its ids given every 16 content tokens and whole at its end, each device submission spinning 30 ms, another conversation's 600-token prompt as it ends, then the next turn), whose next turn must reuse the prompt and the content's whole blocks.
  With the change it reuses 768 of 768, with 0 ids left at the reply's end; the reply's gaps beside the job 33.7 ms mean, 60.2 p95, 61.7 p99, the job about 34 rows a second (Windows, one CPU, synthetic Q8_0 model), and on Linux at the rebased head 33.7, 60.6 and 62.1 ms with 768 of 768.
  `server-resume`'s `trims_finished_donor` (four, seven, two and seven blocks) and `keeps_paused_donor` (a paused request given its next turn's ids takes its donor back whole); `writing_growth` and `reprefilled` give the ids every 20 passes as the routes do; `job_beside_decode` holds each step after passes of the request alone; the costly last-block variant and `server-passes`' budget checks go with the budget.
- **F2DEV's review of 16:28, its three items:** (1) the write cadence above, held by `cache-scenario`'s turn-end write beside a reply (8 segments at reply-only passes 28, 31, 34 ... 49, a lone donor in one write; with segments every round it fails at 1 pass apart); (2) `trim` stops a write of its donor in flight past the kept prefix (`DiskTier::writes_past`, `cancel_write`), and a write the server stopped itself no longer counts as failed: `server-resume`'s `trim_stops_write`, the whole write held at the store across the trim, ends with one file written again and no failure, and fails without the stop (the held write publishing as the only file); (3) `serve_gaps` and `between_auto` share one owner of a boundary's grant and recording (`grant_service`, `record_service`), `serve_gaps` differing only in its count and in having no clock or floor.
- **Run at the rebased head (Linux, two CPUs):** the `cache-scenario` legs (18455 checks) and production script (23 s), `server-passes`, `server-passes-cpu`, `server-resume` cpu-resume and cpu-cache pass; docs and dead-code pass.
- **Left:** the 27B leg once at the final head, the hosted run, F2DEV's review; later, as its own change, the refused directory's removal (DISK-TIER).

No extra timing, broad HF calibration or 16K check is required for this static metadata change. The landing is recorded above.
- **Gotchas:** `bytes` is the logical table size (`rows * row_bytes`), not summed allocations across replicas. File-backed means rows are sourced from the model file; it does not mean the operating system has those pages resident. Prefix-cache disk counters are unrelated to lookup I/O. A CPU backend allocation is host memory, never VRAM. The topology is built after tensor resolution and its JSON is cached when the server API is constructed, then reused in health responses. F2DEV reviewed this as one-time metadata construction and serialization outside per-token inference; no extra timing run is owed for this path. No live hit, miss, lookup latency or I/O metric exists.

## An agent's turn past the context is cut at its tool exchanges (2026-10-22, branch fix/agent-turn-cut on main 2cc7b7453, XDEV's REVIEW of 2026-10-20 10:53, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Why:** on production an agent run's request of 657835 tokens, past the 262144 limit, was refused under `--context-overflow shift` with "its newest turns alone do not fit, so no cut helps". `Api::fit` marked only user messages as turn starts and `first_kept` keeps a whole turn, so the newest turn, a user message and every tool call and result after it, was one unit with nothing left to cut.
- **The change:** where `first_kept` finds no whole turn, `cut_inside` (`context_cut.hpp`) drops the earlier turns and the newest turn's oldest exchanges, each an assistant message with every result after it, so parallel calls and their results stay together and no result is orphaned. The system message and the newest user message stay, and `first_kept` over that view picks the exchange in the same half-limit steps, so successive calls of one agent cut at the same exchange. The kept messages are rendered and tokenized again before acceptance, and the drop is reported as cuts are. A request is refused only where the system and newest user messages alone, or the newest exchange beside them, do not fit; no message is cut inside (the owner's decision, open).
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on main (245 tokens refused on a 128-token pool): `server`'s agent turn of five to nine exchanges, one a parallel pair, cut with its calls and results together, its reply the kept messages', the cut held in pairs as the turn grows (kept from messages 13, 13, 17, 17 and 21), and the two refusals. With the change `context-cut` adds the rule's fixed cases and 20000 random turns against the walk (80195 checks); the ordinary conversation cases are unchanged.
- **Found by the hosted run, fixed here (two commits after the change):** `cache-scenario-production` took 170 s on the Linux runner against 15 s before, twice at this head, and 247 s at main 2cc7b7453 and at this head alike in a two-CPU Linux container, so not this change: after the restart a turn waiting for a donor's write to disk waited out the 15 s bound 15 times, the write never started. `Cache::flush_one` returned at the first donor beyond the host tier that the background budget gave no block, before the donor the request waited for, whose write goes in whole pieces whatever the budget. It now passes such a donor over. The script now holds that no such wait reaches its bound (failing on Linux before the fix), and runs in 23.4 s there.
- **F2DEV's audit of 13:26, the same kind of loop, fixed here (two commits after those):** `Cache::follow_up` admitted only `jobs_.front()` and stopped while that job read its history from disk or was refused room beside running requests, so a younger job that needed neither waited too. It now walks the waiting jobs in order, passing such a job over; the drop of a refused job when nothing runs is unchanged. The legs check both: a younger job completing while an older one's read is held, and while an older one is refused room beside a running request (each failing before the fix, within 20 s and 10 s).
- **Left:** the hosted run, F2DEV's review of the last pair.

- **Goal:** reduce packed-row and prompt-tile unpack work without changing decoded codes, activation arithmetic or range repair. This dependent experiment starts at `307a91d1d`; the qualified runtime remains `e8d1737ee` on its existing branch.

- **Staged and TP4 warm controls:** both used the same four physical GPUs, 12 GiB host cap, production-online setting and int8/F16-KV/MTP configuration as the four-GPU layer control. Each made one P16384/G256 warmup and one identical measured request with zero KV reuse; all raw rows, exact source and harness hashes, rig paths, and activity/process observations are retained in the [record](benchmarks/flash-q4-p16384-warmup-20261020.json). The staged run's MTP accepted/drafted counts were 53/80 on warmup and 74/113 measured; its warmup had 80 disk and one unrelated-CPU flagged interval, while the measured request had no activity flags. TP4 accepted/drafted 45/79 on warmup and 58/95 measured; its warmup had 77 disk and one unrelated-CPU flagged interval, while the measured request had four unrelated-CPU flagged intervals and no disk flags. These are single llmx controls with no new matched mx arm and are not final performance gates.

- **Interpretation:** whole-disk traffic falls from about 649 to 12 MB/s on four cards and 615 to 13 MB/s on six; both measured repeats have zero activity flags. This supports file-page warming as a substantial contributor, not an isolated measurement of PLE or a full-table prefault implementation. The repeats warm only the prompt's selected rows. No global cache was dropped, and the 12 GiB controls are not interchangeable with the 32 GiB matrix.
- **Resident defect:** a separate six-card run explicitly loaded PLE on its device, fitted as layers 0 / 1 / 2-12 / 13-24 / 25-36 / 37-47. Its first PP was 676.305 and repeated mean 706.774, but its output differs from both file controls and MTP produced zero verified drafts despite being configured. These timings are correctness-unqualified and must not be accepted as valid inference performance. Source review found 32-bit byte offsets in `src/backends/vulkan/shaders/embed.comp`: an IQ4_NL row of width 160 occupies 90 bytes, and high rows wrap beyond 4 GiB. The table has 320001536 rows and occupies 28800138240 bytes, about 26.8 GiB. The full table is bound without rebasing; the file path instead uses wide host offsets and remaps small uploaded row packs. Use file-backed PLE on the released runtime until the addressing and descriptor-range fix is qualified.
- **Reproducer:** the independent, four-row Vulkan regression test now confirms the resident gather bug on the released runtime, with the host-ID and device-ID paths each failing all 480 high-row values while low rows and invalid-ID zero controls pass. The exact byte offset 4294968660 wraps to 1364 in 32-bit arithmetic. The authoritative record is `worktrees/vulkan-large-lookup-20261020/docs/benchmarks/vulkan-large-lookup-repro-20261020.json` at commit `6a3adff52fe8d3da76bff750feb2f5c4b4dd32d2`. The separate descriptor-range limit is also confirmed; widening shader arithmetic alone cannot address it.
- **Left:** fix and qualify large resident gather addressing on its own branch, including descriptor range limits. The other developer's eight-thread page-touch warmup work remains separate and its patch was requested on TUI. No such patch or full-host-residency guarantee is part of these runs. Production was restored within its original 45-minute pause window, and stayed online for all four file-backed warmup controls. Flash Q4 production rollout is recorded above.
- **Checkpoint scope:** measurements and documentation only. Runtime, tests and precision budgets are unchanged. The prior 115-page claim review at `b11b01d5a` is carried forward for unchanged material; this checkpoint rechecks current lookup/storage claims, benchmark interpretation, CLI policies and stale progress against the new evidence. ## The cache behind one owner (2026-10-19, branch feat/item14 on feat/rank 1c5247c4b, item 14 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 8, lands by fast-forward as two commits after feat/rank)

- **Why:** the cache's decisions were members of `Scheduler` defined in `reuse.hpp`, so the holders, the round and pacing shared one class and every cache change touched the scheduler (the user's "one tight solution, all in one place").
- **The change (the DESIGN of 19:00, F2DEV's DECISION of 19:02):** the first commit moves the holders, their types, the cache's counters, admission's cache part, parking, the jobs and the 63 functions `reuse.hpp` held into `class Cache` in `src/server/cache.hpp`, which the scheduler holds as `cache_` and calls; no body changes but `next_disk_bound` losing its `const`, and the scheduler's own `Held` losing the `operator*` the move left unused (the linked dead-code check of run 39332012407), held by a per-function diff against 1c5247c4b. The second commit changes call sites only, so the cache is no view of the scheduler: the pools, the seats, the host tier's bytes, the request limit, the waits' bounds and the server's start are values set at construction; `running_` is gone and `room`, `served` and the eleven functions that reach `room` take the active list, and the ten that search the queued and paused requests, with the nine that reach them (`park`, `prove`, `settle_disk` among them), take the waiting lines (`Cache::Lines`); the round grants a write's pieces through `grant_writes`, which hands back what the last pieces cost; the stop's flush is handed the scheduler's condition; the idle moment, `taken_back_` and `admissions_` are the cache's; the scheduler hands in its measured prompt rate and its stop, and stores the active count after a request's `park`. Then, at F2DEV's review of 20:30, the outward boundary: the scheduler reaches `Cache` only through calls (`fill` for the cache's half of the stats, `stop` for the shutdown, `open_disk` for the disk tier from the options and a wake function, `keeps`, `idle_moment` with the scheduler's condition, read in `disk_round`, `job_rows_read`, and a few more the compiler named: `due`, `woken`, `grow_ahead`, `follow`, `leave`, and `take` and `evict` for the donors a growing request takes, the one paused by its id from `park`), the hold comes as constructor arguments, and every other member is private, the class reordered into its public calls and the rest with no line changed.
- **What the cache still shares:** the model and the lock, as designed; the hold of the stages comes as two functions the scheduler hands in (`hold_`, `unhold_`), and the measured prompt rate and the stop as values it sets.

## One ranking of what stays (2026-10-19, branch feat/rank on stack/cache-top 1371d9a60, item 10 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 8, step 7 with step 9's cut part, lands by fast-forward as two commits after the stack)

- **Why:** each tier picked its victims by its own order (N12): `make_room` oldest first, the donor count three loops, `host_room` five passes and a refusal counter, `release_written` and two `drop_oldest`, `keep_boundary`'s fixed count of four states a conversation (N15) and `checkpoint_room_held` the oldest slot holder; none asked whether its victim was the last holder of its rows, a boundary without rows held its place (N6), and the donor count could give up a donor whose turn-end write was running (A19).
- **The change (the DESIGN of 16:38, F2DEV's DECISION of 16:41):** `Scheduler::rank`, one key for a device donor, a host copy or a boundary: class 0 where its going loses nothing (superseded, orphaned by a cut, a boundary without its rows, rows another holder keeps or whole on disk), 1 a conversation that did not come back, 2 one that did, each least recently used first; `Donor` gets the `used` stamp the others have, set as it is parked and forked, and a copy keeps its donor's. `make_room` takes the donors' order (`ranked`, a donor whose write is in flight last) in place of a count; the donor count parks the newcomer and gives up the lowest-ranked; `host_room`, `keep_boundary`, the proof's and a read's room release host entries in rank order below the newcomer's own (`host_victims`, `host_room_for`, ranked again after each drop); `write_ahead` writes the entry the ranking would drop next, its three-quarters trigger kept; `checkpoint_room_held` gives up the lowest slot holder. `writing` asks `DiskTier::writing_of`, which now matches the file in flight's last block as well as the digest below it: the digests being a chain, histories that share a start share every digest below where they part, from the root below a file at row 0 up, so before, any donor counted as being written while one such file was, and with the first block alone two conversations under one system prompt still would (F2DEV, 02:43) (run 39353206254, where A's donor was given up and its repeat read A's file back), and the wait for a donor's write read another history's progress the same way. `kBoundaries`, `host_refused_`, `release_written`, `drop_oldest_bound`, `drop_oldest_host` and `kept_elsewhere` are gone. A cut's request carries the uncut prompt through its first dropped row (`Api::fit`, `submit`), and admission supersedes every holder of that row. `held_below` passes over the holder going, so a refused write-back gives its rows as lost where it counted itself as their holder.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on 1371d9a60 (the returning leg's P3: the two conversations lost their rows to the one-offs): many users at the cap restated as two conversations coming back every round beside four one-off requests, which keep every row (held), the pure six-way cycle kept as a recorded count (1152 rows a conversation, as before); the hybrid scenario's edit at 768 of 768 and the older edit at 512 on one CPU and over two, where a state now takes a copy's room (N15); `server-resume`'s cut ranking the uncut history out (failing with the marking off: the older X's repeat reused 0) and the donor count keeping a donor whose held write is in flight (A19); `server-passes` `make_room` over an order by hand. In the change commit three witnesses move with the ranking: message boundaries keep six states, not four; with host memory for one copy the repeat's copy outranks every newcomer, so the newcomer's repeat forks nothing and the repeat's 384; and the recorder rule's promoted conversation is the one step 0 came back to, the newest one's donor being the last holder of its rows. N6 has no case of its own (F2DEV, 17:58): a boundary without rows ranks with class 0 by the rule, and a case sized to make it the victim needed host sizing the states' slabs do not give; one is owed if the health shows boundaries piling up.
- **The cut and the restart said with their cost (item 11, F2DEV's DECISION of 18:01, one commit after the ranking):** a request carrying a cut says once at admission `server: cache: a cut turn reads R rows again beside S reused`, with the seconds at the measured prompt rate once a pass has measured it (P5); a kept directory refused for its identity says its entries and MiB, computed again where a turn needs them, from `DiskStore`'s own walk (P4's clause). No move, count or health field. The scenario's cut leg passes its cut as the routes do, and its log gives the line at each cut turn with the leg's own classification, 616 rows again beside 384 reused; `disk-store`'s refused directory holds one entry and its refusal names it.
- **Left:** the hosted run, reviews.

## The cut prompt's cases hold the cut's start, not a time (2026-10-19, tests only, one commit under item 10's tests)

- **Why:** gate/cache-rest's hosted run 39332012407 failed `server-passes-cpu` on Windows: "a prompt cut by its pieces' time: ... the longest attention past 1400 tokens 172.2 ms ..., against some and at most 100 ms". The bound of 100 ms, twice `kPieceMs`, predates the search, whose target is the longest of `kPieceMs`, the reply's own pass and the probe's piece and `kPieceMs` more (`PieceSearch::target`), so on a runner whose probe or reply pass is slow the slices legitimately grow past it; that runner's longest piece took 248.9 ms.
- **The change:** the prompt cut by its pieces' time and the prompt at a new depth no longer bound the longest deep attention; they still print it, and still hold what the search fixes: the probe of one step alone in its pass, the first slice past 1400 tokens being that probe, the record's shape and every reply its reply alone.
- **The staircase case too:** gate/cache-rest's run at ffd21d398 failed it on macOS with slices of 16, 32, 64, 128, 96, 112 and 44 rows, the search halving its bracket after 128 was over (96, then 112), which its "no growth after the turn down" forbade though the rule does it. It now holds the rule's claim: the probe, its double, doubling up to the first slice over the target, then every slice between the last within the target and that one, the prompt's last alone shorter; Windows gave 16, 32, 64, then 48 to the end and 44.
- **Held by:** `server-passes-cpu` on Windows; the hosted run of the gate branch.

## The first write's case counts the other history's file, not its bytes (2026-10-19, branch stack/cache-top, tests only, one commit on the stack)

- **Why:** the stack's hosted run 39307121297 timed out in `cache-scenario` on ubuntu-24.04, as feat/kv-pool's run 39135787656 had failed on macOS (Why of the record of 2026-10-18 below, which took it for a slow runner): after its two requests the first-write case waited for the bytes written to reach twice what they were once the first history was whole, but that history goes to disk in one write or two as the background budget falls while the second request waits for it, and the store pads each write, so where it took two (both failing runs queued the second request about 6.6 and 7.1 s, two of the store's 3 s holds) the other history's one write never reached the mark and nothing else is written. On Windows the first history takes one write of 2 MiB and the other one of 2 MiB.

- **Held by:** the legs on Windows; the hosted run of github gate/cache-top.

## One question for reuse (2026-10-19, branch feat/item8 on feat/a21 826de2732, item 8 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 8, step 6's remainder, lands by fast-forward as two commits after A21)

- **Why:** `enter` asked five searches in turn, `prefetch` three of them and never the running requests and jobs (N3), `hand_jobs` two and `rows_held` a fourth walk; a failed promotion or a boundary that lost its rows fell back to the best donor rather than the next restore point (N8, N9); two followers of one history on disk read it twice (gap 6); and a job started before `prefetch` looked at it, computing what the files held (gap 5).
- **The change (the DESIGN of 15:39, F2DEV's DECISION of 15:41):** `Scheduler::served` in `reuse.hpp`, a pure question giving the longest restore point memory holds of a history and its holder (`Served`): device donors, host entries, boundaries whose rows a donor or host entry not passed over holds, and with `running` the running sources `enter` forks. `enter` asks it and acts on the holder, a holder that fails (a promotion, a boundary's rows, its checkpoint slot) going into a skip set and the question asked again, once a holder, with the existing pins; `prefetch`, `hand_jobs`, `held_below` and the state read ask it too, the state read keeping the renewal and rotation of the host entry it relies on. `best_donor`, `best_bound`, `best_host` and `rows_held` are gone. A read into host memory already reading the same rows serves a second request, by the match streams use, and a waiter leaving leaves the read as before. A job's read is asked over all its ids and decided by the blocks `enter` would take (its need less what memory serves); one that could not start now is left to `enter`'s own rule, and a job does not start before `prefetch` has looked at it (`reading`). The disk store's test hook gains a read's chunk (`fault("read")`), which the leaving case holds.
- **Tests:** the first commit, failing on 826de2732: the restart leg's two expectations flip to held (one read for two followers, `reads` 2 to 1; the job reading its 256 rows from disk, computing none), the same leg with one follower leaving while both wait for the held read and the other served whole, and `server-resume`'s promotion failing once (`FailingCopies::fail_writes`), where the third turn forks the first turn's 256 rows (0 on 826de2732). In the change commit `server-resume`'s restart into a host tier smaller than an entry reads 3 or 4 entries back, where it read 3: the second conversation's job now reads its history back as a request does, before the count is taken or after it as its round falls (the hosted run of the stack read 3 on Linux and Windows). A job joining the line again (giving way, handed back, its ids changed) is looked at again (`disk_checked_` and `looked_` cleared), one that found no room is not marked looked at so a later look can read for it, and `reading` holds a job only until `prefetch` has looked at it once, so one that never finds room by the look still starts by `enter`'s rule (F2DEV, 16:10). Room-once's two partial-eviction witnesses are held to a range, B paused past its step at 512 and before 640, after one local run paused it at 531 (403 rows, against 404): where A's step pauses B follows how their passes fall.
- **Left:** the hosted run, reviews.

## A job with one block left reads it while the request it would give way to waits for a write (2026-10-19, branch feat/a21 on the stack gate/cache-stack 1de1dbc94, item 9 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 8, A21, lands by fast-forward as two commits after the stack)

- **Why:** run D's read-ahead job gave way with its last block unread to a request that did not fit beside it and then waited for a donor's write in any case, so the next turn computed those rows (64, about 1 s at 238k).
- **The change (the DESIGN of 15:21, F2DEV's DECISION of 15:23):** `enter`'s test for the donor whose write a request would wait for is one function, `awaited_write`, which `enter` asks unchanged. In the round, where a waiting request does not fit, `waits_for_write` plans its room as `admits` does with the running jobs counted as freed (`gain_of` now takes several sequences going in any case), and where `awaited_write` names a donor `yield_jobs` spares each job with at most one block left to its ids' last whole block; it reads that block and completes as any job does. The spare has no clock, by construction: it is one block of rows at most, and it ends with the write, which the next round's check no longer names; the request's own wait starts in `enter` once the job has gone, with its bound as before (F2DEV, 15:23). `waits_for_write` plans with no forked donor, as `admits` does, so it may spare a job where `enter` would not wait, at a cost of at most one block of one job, or miss a write `enter` would wait for where the donor the request forks is the oldest, which leaves the job giving way as it did before (F2DEV, 15:36, the second case the developer's). A write's chunk asks the disk store's test hook (`DiskStore::Options::fault`, step `write`), which a test holds.
- **Tests:** `cache-scenario`'s job with its last block left, the first commit, failing on 1de1dbc94 (the job gave way and the next turn reused 640 rows, against 768): with the donor's write held by the hook and the passes held at retirement, the job completes and the next turn reuses 768; with the write let go and whole after one spared round, the job gives way (`job_gave_way` 1); with the donor whole on disk before the request, it gives way at once; each reply its reply alone. `awaited_write`'s donors are met there: one written in flight, one whole on disk and one superseded (the turn's, once the job's donor stands for it); the forked one is `enter`'s, unchanged.
- **Left:** the hosted run, reviews.

## Room counted once (2026-10-19, branch feat/room-once on step1b/legs 84e6ff9da, item 7 of docs/CACHE-PLAN.md section 8, step 3, lands by fast-forward as two commits after step1b/legs)

- **Why:** the scheduler's ledger (`reserved_`) added each request's whole reservation and each donor's whole blocks, so blocks a fork shares with its donor were counted twice: a conversation past half the pool could not keep two holders (N1, S1's root) and a donor forked by an edit was consumed for room, its rows past the fork lost (N14).
- **The change (the DESIGN of 13:28, F2DEV's DECISION of 13:31):** one count of the device's room in `reuse.hpp`. `room()` is each pool's free blocks in the model less what the running requests promised and have not taken (`need_` less what their sequences hold, a pass's prepared blocks among them, so a request in flight counts at what its pass took). `Model::freed(set)` (history.hpp) says what a set of sequences frees together, from the pool's own references, blocks and checkpoint slots. `make_room` takes the free blocks and a `Gain` asked of the cumulative victim set, never victim by victim, and gives back only a donor that frees nothing beside the other victims, the order otherwise unchanged. `reserved_`, its eleven add and sub sites, `Donor::blocks`, `donor_blocks()` and `Streaming::need` are gone. `Stats::reserved` keeps its name with the true count (taken or promised) and `donor_blocks` is what only donors and streams hold, both as `note_room` last found them. Marks stay outside, the host and disk tiers' room untouched.
- **One more change the count needed:** of donors sharing as much with a request, `best_donor` takes the newest. A request no longer consumes a donor it shares whole, so two donors of one conversation can stand, the older inside the newer, and a job forking the older found no room the newer could give; the newer, a fork of the older, holds all it holds.
- **Tests:** the failing commit flips the scenario's two expectations to held: a turn's donor beside its job past half the pool, and a donor forked by an edit losing no row (the next turn reusing all 1152 on the synthetic model, its split and the hybrid model, where it was 896 and 768). `kv-cache` holds `Model::freed` against the pool on one pool and two, `arch-qwen35` a checkpoint's slot a fork shares, `server-passes` the set gain by hand beside its simulation (whose ledger shares nothing, through an adapter), donors still taken oldest first where the newer alone would do, and a donor that frees nothing beside the others given back. step1b's room-for-all and room-for-four legs are unchanged.
- **Witnesses the count moved, in the change's commit:** `server-resume`'s request whose donor went with part of its history kept, and its twin beside a donor holding its reply as prompt rows, now take their step at 512 tokens with the setup's donor (its one unshared block the gain), so A's step pauses B at 532 and the resume recomputes 404 rows, not 384, still forking the first block alone. The two stop cases of item 14 (`stop_keeps_job`, `stop_keeps_request`) no longer take the donor over, since a fork sharing every block of its donor frees nothing by consuming it: they keep that shape, the donor beside the job or the request, and each runs again as the only holder (F2DEV's REVIEW of 14:41), on the synthetic model, where three other turns ending at three requests at once make the donor count drop the turn's donor while the job reads or the request replies, the stop then held at a pass and the restart required to fork the 512 tokens only the job or request held. With the stop's parking reverted locally each lone case fails, the restart forking 256; the hybrid model is not used for them, as a job there parks at the checkpoint it forked, which the dropped donor's host copy also holds. The test's gate lets attention calls go one at a time (`HeldAttention::hold_until`), so the stop is taken at the first held call after the scheduler's counts show the donor dropped, not after a time.
- **Left:** the gate (host logic: CTest, the CPU suite, Qwen3-0.6B identity against main, the hosted run; the scenario legs; on the 27B, S8's turn after a task keeping two holders past half the pool), reviews.

## A restore from disk streamed to the devices (2026-10-18, branch fix/streamed-restore, A20, in progress)

- **Goal:** a history larger than the host tier read from disk straight into its device storage through the read ring, with no whole host copy (the DESIGN of 2026-10-17 06:06 with XDEV's three points of 10:13, and the UPDATE of 2026-10-18 15:06), so a restart whose host memory holds no whole copy still reuses its kept history.
- **Done (the two commits, not yet reviewed):** the failing case (`server-resume`'s restart with host memory for no whole copy, failing on main with "not read back (no host memory for the copy beside the reserve the host keeps)"); the read ring as one object (`infer::ReadRing`), the loader's stream on it with `load-progress` unchanged and the ring stepped without waiting; the model's restore by destinations (`Model::restore_into`, `restored`, `host_layout`), bit-identical to `restore_host` on one CPU dense and hybrid and over two CPU stages; the store's checks for a read off its thread (`DiskStore::open_entry`, `read_chunk`, `drop_entry`); the tier's streamed read (`StreamedRead`, `DiskTier::stream`, `end_stream`, its files pinned); the scheduler's filled donor (`start_stream`, `stream_round`, a cancel at the bound of every request waiting, the round looking again a millisecond on while a stream runs, which `server-resume`'s streamed restore on a device whose copies retire after their submission holds); a stream starts only once the devices have its room, looked at again each round rather than refused, so a request whose room is busy still reads its history once it frees; a stream already reading a request's rows serves it, and streams count among the reads in flight; no restore job for the donor a restore job's donor evicts from the one slot (`restoring_`), which had two conversations' jobs trade it forever under `--max-seqs 1`; the through host copy removed, `start_read` streaming a history larger than the whole host tier (`HostDonor::through`, its `parked_held` share and its `!through` conditions gone); a restore's KV runs find their buffer at each copy (`RestoreInto::Run::target`), since another history's pass that grows the storage between chunks replaced the buffers the runs named, which crashed or lost rows on a layer split (`kv-cache` holds it: a restore whose storage grows before its copies); the read's slot views made under the hold; the restart cases (`disk_kept`'s, the boundary arm with no host memory, the recorder rule's fifth step) expecting the streamed read; the stream's faults on the restart case: a flipped byte fails the read and frees its room, a turn cancelled mid-read leaves the stream to serve the same turn sent again, and a stop mid-read ends both (the store's pace now holds a streamed chunk too); ## The slow write's two arms independent of the runner (2026-10-18, branch test/capped-write-wait, tests only, lands by fast-forward as one commit)

- **Why:** both arms of `cache-scenario`'s slow write failed on macOS. The capped arm (fix/turns-kept's run 39135787891, "1 waits, 0 at their bound"): its 100 ms bound is seen only at the scheduler's next look, which on a slow runner came after the write, whose pieces the store held 200 ms each, had ended. The uncapped arm (feat/restore-ms's run 39156576100, "1 waits, 1 at their bound"): a wait for a donor's write follows the write's rate only once that write has begun (`waits_for_room` reads the write in flight); the other request arrived before this runner had begun it, so the wait had only its 100 ms constant, as the line "left the devices with no copy ... not yet whole on disk" 154 ms in shows.
- **The change:** the capped arm's store holds each piece five minutes, so the write is in flight at any look a running scheduler makes and the wait is counted at its bound; the uncapped arm's holds each piece five seconds, and the other request is submitted once the history's write is under way (`Stats::disk_in_flight`), so the wait follows the write's rate whatever the runner. Both checks stay on counts; the stop cancels the capped write, so neither case takes long.
- **Held by:** the legs four copies at once on Windows, every run passing in 59 s; CTest; the hosted run of github gate/capped-write-wait.
