### A generating request beside a prompt: the layer split, and what the automatic rule leaves open

- **Goal:** a request already generating is served while prompts are read, on every placement, without a number for the user to choose.
- **Done:** one device and one tensor group, by the automatic rule as the default there, with `--no-pacing` to turn it off and the fixed share kept as its control (the record of 2026-10-12 below, with its matrix; the fixed share's record of 2026-10-09).
- **Left:** a layer split, which is not paced and refuses a fixed share: fed in pieces a prompt's pass stays in flight for its stage's device time, and a sequence is in one pass at a time, so the stages would stop overlapping on the prompt. The repair is a sequence in consecutive passes at consecutive stages (`docs/MULTI-DEVICE.md`, order of work, 4), then the share's table on a split. A stage on the CPU, which computes as it is recorded, is not fed in pieces. Open on the paced placements, each named in the record of 2026-10-12: with the embedded drafter a service is long and the prompt reads 1.74 times main's time, the split the owner chose with the floor at one half, which is the constant to revisit if prompts prove too slow; at 64 users most gaps are above the target and first tokens wait longer than on main; one 8.1 s pause after a prompt in one early run is unexplained; a second overlap from a resumed request, a late hold at a grant and a delay between a grant's offer and its taking up have no scheduler case; and the Radeon VII's pieces and gaps are not measured, only its tests run.
- **Gotchas:** the price of a pass of generated rows leans low, the least of a stage's last eight, so rows go apart a little more often than an exact price would send them, toward the generating request. While rows ride a prompt's passes their price is not measured, so a ride is bounded by a pass apart after eight prompt passes (`RideRun`) and not by its price. The time a stage stands still for the scheduler's own device work is spent by whoever generates on that stage, also when the work is another request's copy to host memory; what they owe for it stops at two passes. A pass's cost counts from the last pass of its own kind, since passes apart retire past the others. The chain beside a recording on the head's device draws no sanitizer report on CPU groups, so its wait has coverage and no failing case.

### The tensor split on every model the layer split serves

- **Goal:** `--tensor-width N` runs each family the layer split runs, with its gates: the hybrid qwen35 models (Qwen 3.5, 3.6 and 3.8), then an embedded drafter over a group, then routed experts (qwen3moe, qwen35moe); the plan's steps 5, 6 and 8 (`docs/TENSOR-SPLIT.md`, section 6).
- **Done:** the hybrid models (branch feat/tp-qwen35, its record below): a linear-attention layer on each member over its K heads and the V heads that read them, each member keeping the recurrent state of those heads under the slot ids the group shares, so checkpoints, marks, the rerun after a retract, the host tier's copies and drafting by lookup run over a group. The embedded drafter (branch feat/tp-spec, its record below): each member its shards of the MTP block and the head whole for a draft row, with no join of the members' argmax. Routed experts (branch feat/tp-moe, its record below): each member its share of every expert's hidden rows beside the whole router. Covering blocks (branch feat/tp-moe-cover, its record below): the K-quant files whose expert width does not split on whole blocks.
- **Left:** the join of the members' argmax in `Collective` if a draft row's head shows in a profile; the open speed cells of each record.
- **Gotchas:** a member's activation slots keep one device's widths, so its arena is larger than it needs by the share it does not use; the fit counts it as allocated.

### Drafting: combined proposers, and what a draft costs by phase

- **Goal:** more tokens a pass with the output of the run without drafts, greedy and seeded, on every placement: lookup first where a request's own history convinces, the model drafter otherwise, a lookup tail after a model draft, and draft models in the server; each step built only on a measured gain ([SPECULATIVE](SPECULATIVE.md), sections 3 and 7).
- **Done:** `argmax_rows` reduces a long row in slices (branch perf/argmax-rows, its record above). A reply's own history drafted ahead of a model drafter, an acceptance record a source (branch feat/lookup-first, its record above). Step 1, the timing split (branch perf/draft-timing): `bench --model --drafter embedded` times a chain and a verify at each draft count to `--draft-max`, `--profile` gives each of them by kernel with the output head's products on lines of their own and reads every listed Vulkan device, and `serve --timing` gives the scheduler thread's time in the chains and in the verifies' retracts.
- **Left:** a draft of the history up to 7 tokens with the pass price learning cost by width; draft models in the server, their histories found by tokens inside `spec::DraftModel` and caught up in bounded pieces outside the price; a block drafter, for which a file exists (a `dflash` drafter of Qwen3.8-27B), as a new architecture module with its reference named first. Measured and not built: a lookup tail after a model draft and a lookup probe after a refused one, a reduced draft head, a five- or six-column decode build, and a draft row's logits in device memory (0.02 ms a row for the argmax against 0.08 on an MI50, under half a percent of a round, the head's product the same in either memory).
- **Gotchas:** the head's line and a profile of several devices need a Vulkan device, which no hosted runner has, so they are checked by hand with `llmx bench --model FILE --device vulkan:0 --drafter embedded --profile` on one device and with two devices under `--tensor-width 2`; the hosted suite holds the `bench: draft` lines on the CPU. What the head's override costs a backend that times nothing is read from the gate's timing round against main (one branch a head call), and that it changes no output from the identity run on a device.

## A lone request stalled by its own reply's job takes its step in the same round (2026-10-13, branch fix/stalled-alone, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found by a gate run:** on Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M, one MI50, `--ctx-size 8192`, an uncapped chat of 2773 prompt tokens ended after about 2500 tokens with HTTP 500, `server: a round with active requests formed an empty pass`, on main as on the branch under test.
- **The smallest form, no device:** Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M on the CPU, `--ctx-size 2048`, one greedy `/v1/chat/completions` without `max_tokens` on a 695-token prompt ends with that error after 330 tokens, 3 runs of 3 on main a6f72aa75. Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Q4_0, a dense model, ends the same way after 328 tokens of a 697-token prompt, 1 run.
- **First bad commit:** 42dca4051 of 2026-10-01, the reply read again as prompt rows. On the CPU form its parent 395b49504 runs to the end of the reply (883 tokens), it fails, and 7d15a2f07, before the default pacing, and a6f72aa75 fail at the same token; `--no-pacing` fails the same, so pacing has no part. On the device, with a prompt of 2771 tokens, each of eight commits from 395b49504 to a6f72aa75 ran to the end without a stall: whether the device meets it depends on where the job's reservation stands when the step falls due.
- **Cause:** a lone uncapped request holds its history and one growth step. The job that reads its reply again as it is written reserves the blocks of all its ids. When the two fill the pool and the request's next token passes its blocks, `grow` finds no room, the job being neither a donor nor a request to pause, and marks the request stalled. The round then made the job give way, which freed the room, but growth had run for that round: the request sat the pass out, the job was gone, nothing was formed and nothing was in flight, and the round's check ended every active request with the error. Before the jobs a stalled request always waited on another request's pass.
- **Done:** where a request could not grow and a job gave way for it, the growth steps run again in that round for the stalled requests alone (`grow` with `again`), so the request takes the room and is in the pass. A stall is counted where it still stands after the last call that could lift it, so `pressure.since_start.stalls` stays the passes a request sat out. `yield_jobs` says whether a job gave way. The check is untouched; its error now names the request left without a pass, whether it could not grow, the active requests and each pool's reserved blocks.
- **The failing case first:** `server-resume`, `stalled_alone`: a 700-token prompt on 16 blocks, the next turn's ids given once 250 tokens are written, the request running uncapped to its limit with the ids and values of its reply alone, a job given way and no pass sat out; on the synthetic Q8_0 model and on the hybrid one. On main both end with the error. A third form runs two such requests whose steps fall due in one round, asserted from the retired passes; it passes on main too, since the older request's step pauses the younger and neither is left stalled with nothing in flight, and it is kept as a guard on the second growth with several requests.
- **Not in the device half of `server-resume`:** that half has no hybrid model and its model's blocks are 64 tokens, where the case's numbers are for 128; the defect is in the host's round and no device code is on its path. `server-passes`, the policy simulation, has no jobs and holds nothing here.
- **Why a chat of 250000 tokens on a 262144-token pool did not meet it:** a job is admitted only where the blocks of all its ids are free or held by donors (`enter` pauses no one for it), so a conversation above about half the pool gets no job while its request runs, and without a job nothing holds the room its step needs. Exposed was a chat whose history and reply, counted twice, reach the pool: about half the pool of conversation, or a shorter one with a long reply.
- **A request with `max_tokens` does not meet it, by a run:** it reserves its whole reply at admission and takes no growth step. The CPU form on main with `max_tokens` 500 ran its 500 tokens, past the 330 where the uncapped one ended, with a job admitted beside it (128 rows read again) and no stall; with 1200 and 1300 it ran to the end of the reply, 869 tokens, and no job was admitted, the request's own reservation leaving no room for one. One run each.
- **Other ways to a round that forms nothing with nothing in flight, read from the round at this head:** a request in flight leaves a pass flying; a stall that waits on a victim in flight likewise; a request whose history is read from disk or whose proof is pending waits in the queue, not among the active; jobs alone are left out by the check. What remains is every active request stalled at once with no job to give way, which needs the oldest request's step to fail after every donor is taken and every younger uncapped request paused, and admission and the step's clamp to the pool keep a request's own history and step within the pool. So after this change the check holds an invariant and not a wait: a stalled request with nothing in flight has nothing left that could free room, and a round that waited there would hang the request where the error ends it with its numbers. None of the active requests is in a pass then and none can be, so ending all of them is what is left. No change to the check is proposed.
- **Left:** a job reserves all its ids beside the request it follows, so a long reply's job and its request compete for the pool until the job gives way; whether a job should be bounded by what the request's next steps leave is not looked at.
- **The gate run's reproduction, at the head before its last rebase and the main it sat on, the source equal:** Qwen3.5-0.8B Q4_K_M on the CPU, 4 threads, `--ctx-size 2048`, greedy, a 695-token prompt, no `max_tokens` unless stated; the dense rows are Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Q4_0 with a 697-token prompt.

  | Arm | Runs | HTTP | Generated tokens | Ended | Stalls | Rows read again, jobs given way |
  |---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---|
  | main | 3 | 500, the empty pass | 330 each | error, sat out 1 pass | 1 | 256, 1 |
  | this change | 3 | 200 | 869 each | end of text | 0 | 256, 1 |
  | main, dense | 1 | 500, the same text | 328 | error, sat out 1 pass | 1 | 256, 1 |
  | this change, dense | 1 | 200 | 1351 | the 2048-token context | 0 | 256, 1 |
  | main, `max_tokens` 500 | 1 | 200 | 500 | length | 0 | 128, 0 |
  | this change, `max_tokens` 500 | 1 | 200 | 500 | length | 0 | 128, 0 |

  No request was paused and no token recomputed in any run. `server-resume` failed at the first commit with the error and passed at the head, its CPU half five times; under ThreadSanitizer it gave no report.

## The fit counts a verify's draft rows (2026-10-12, branch fix/drafted-logits-rows, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found in review of the pacing change, on the main before it:** a server with a drafter reserves 64 draft rows a pass beside a ubatch and a row a request (`Scheduler::kDraftRows`), in its activation arena and in each logits ring, and `open_model` asked the fit for neither: the arena for a ubatch and the requests' rows, the logits for a row a request. So the fitted KV budget left the head's device short by 64 rows of logits a ring, 64 times the vocabulary times 4 bytes, and each device by 64 arena rows. No failure was observed from it; it is an accounting defect found by reading.
- **Done:** the scheduler says what a pass carries (`Scheduler::draft_rows`, `logits_a_pass`), and reserves by it; `open_model` gives the fit the same, `PlacementRequest::draft_rows` for the arena and the logits rows of a pass with its drafts; `infer::fitted_rows` is the one place the fit's rows of a pass are summed. Sequence counts and state slots are unchanged.
- **The failing test first:** `placement` holds `fitted_rows` to a ubatch, the decode rows, the draft rows and the second arena's where a stage is fed in pieces, and `server-passes-cpu` holds the scheduler's rows of a pass with and without drafts; both name what the fix adds and do not build on the main before it. The behavioural case is in `server-passes-cpu`: a model fitted to a device's free memory as the command line asks, then a scheduler with a drafter made over it, allocates within that memory and no more than the same server without a drafter, at a size chosen just below a KV block's edge; fitted with the draft rows left out of a pass's rows, alone or with the logits rows as before the fix, it allocates three KV blocks more, and with them left out of the logits rows alone, a quarter of a block on that model, one block more, each of which the case requires to see. The request is built in the test as `open_model` builds it, so the command line's own wiring is covered by reading only.
- **Found by that case:** the hosted macOS job crashed once in it, on a fault of the scheduler's and not of this change, a stage's thread started with the slot its record is kept in; fixed on its own, in the record below, and this change lands on top of that fix.
- **Left:** one owner for the server's fields of a placement request, a scheduler function that fills them and that the command line and the test both call, so the two cannot drift; the stand-in reviewer's recommendation, a change of its own.
- **Effect on a fitted budget:** with a drafter the KV budget a server is fitted to is smaller by what those rows take; not measured on a real model.
- **Gates:** run and read by the gate runner at the landing head, with its hosted run; the change lands on its green result.
- **Reviewed:** the finding and the request for a behavioural case are the reviewer's; the stand-in gating reviewer approved the change with that case and asked whether each half of the fix is seen alone, which the third size answers.
## A stage's thread is given its record (2026-10-12, branch fix/stage-thread-start, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found by a hosted macOS run:** `server-passes-cpu` segfaulted once on the macOS job of a branch under review, in a new case that makes a scheduler and destroys it at once. `Scheduler` started each stage's thread with the place its record is kept in, a slot of `recorders_`, which the thread reads when it first runs. A scheduler destroyed before that is destroying the slot: the C++ library of the macOS build empties a `unique_ptr` before it deletes what it held, so the late thread read null; the libraries of the Linux and Windows builds delete first, and deleting joins the thread, so there the read still found the record and neither repeated runs nor the thread sanitizer showed anything.
- **Proof of cause, by a prediction posted before the runs:** two measurement-only branches that start a stage's thread 200 ms late, so the destructor always wins. On the unfixed source the macOS job segfaulted in `server-passes-cpu` (hosted run 38288449145) while Linux passed, plain and under the thread sanitizer; with the thread given its record the macOS job passed (hosted run 38288446625).
- **Done:** the thread is given its record (`Recorder*`), not its slot.
- **Reach:** on main since stages have threads. A serving process makes one scheduler and runs it, so it does not meet this. Met by tests, and by a start that fails after the scheduler is made and before it runs, or inside its constructor after the threads are started; the change covers those too, since in each the thread now holds its record until the record's destructor joins it.
- **The failing test first:** `server-passes-cpu` makes and destroys a scheduler with a stage thread 400 times. It asserts nothing: the fault is a crash, and on Linux and Windows the library's order hides it, so the case fails first only in the hosted macOS job, and there by chance of scheduling; the two probe runs above are what shows the cause.
- **Gates:** run and read by the gate runner at the landing head, with its hosted run.
- **Reviewed:** by the stand-in gating reviewer; its verdict at the landing head is a condition of landing.

## A chat at the context's edge keeps room for its reply (2026-10-12, branch feat/reply-room, lands by fast-forward)

- **Seen on production:** under `--context-overflow shift` on a 262144-token context a chat reached 260507 prompt tokens. The prompt fit, so nothing was cut, and the reply got the 1637 tokens left and ended at its limit mid-sentence, turn after turn. A request that names no `max_tokens` counted as fitting down to its last row.
- **Done:** what fits is one rule with one owner, `Scheduler::prompt_room`: the limit less the tokens a request asks for, or less an eighth of the limit (`kReplyRoom`) where it names none. `Api::fit` cuts to it and `submit` refuses past it; the two copies of the old rule, in the route and in `submit`, are gone. So under `shift` an uncapped chat is cut when it passes seven eighths of the limit, by the steps of half the limit it was cut by before, keeps about three eighths and is cut again half the limit later. `/v1/health` counts the cuts (`requests.since_start.shifts`, `shifted_tokens`); the server's line and the reply's `context` object were there. A capped request's room stays its own `max_tokens`; it is not bounded for it.
- **Why an eighth, and no floor:** it is a fraction so the cadence is the same at any context: a cut reads about three eighths of the limit again to buy half. A count of tokens would be right at one context only, and a client that wants another room sends `max_tokens`. No measurement of reply lengths stands behind it.
- **A hole the room opened, closed here:** a cut is counted in whole steps past the leading block, and a system message of three eighths of the limit or more beside an uncapped chat leaves no cut point a whole step past it, so the chat was refused under `shift` although dropping messages would fit. The reviewer found its second half: a step that has a cut point whose window does not fit, with the next step past the prompt's end, was refused the same way. Wherever no whole step serves the cut is now the first cut point after the leading block that leaves at most the room, on the chat routes (`first_kept`, a user start) and the text routes (`cut_rows`); a text prompt in that case used to be cut by rows after a fixed 64-row lead or reported as not fitting, and now keeps its leading block. A prompt is refused under `shift` only where the leading block and its newest turn together do not fit.
- **A change in the default mode:** under `refuse` an uncapped prompt that fits but leaves less than the eighth is now answered 413 with its numbers and the ways out, where it was answered with a reply cut short. In docs/USAGE.md and docs/OPERATING.md.
- **What a cut costs:** the turn that cuts reads the kept window again, about three eighths of the limit, 98000 tokens at 262144; only the system message's whole blocks are forked. Cutting at a KV block's edge and not at a message would reuse no more: reuse is by an equal prefix from row 0, and every kept row sits at a new position after other rows. On a model that keeps a state the system message itself is forked only with a checkpoint at its last whole block, which nothing keeps there, so the turn that first cuts reads from row 0; the next turn of the same window forks it, 4160 of 4218 tokens in the gate run on Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M.
- **The failing tests first:** `context-cut` (the large system message cut and not refused), the suite's `server` component on the synthetic chat model with a pool of 128 (the edge chat refused by default and cut under `shift`, the health counters, the stream's `context`), and `server-passes-cpu` holding the rule at `submit` with no route. On main the first two fail and the third does not build.
- **Not built or not covered, said plainly:** a tool call across the cut and a conversation shifted twice at the same message are held at the row level in `context-cut` and by the capped chat's existing case, not by a new end-to-end case; the hybrid model's shifted turn was not in a test of the suite; the gate run sent the cut prompt of a shifted turn on Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M to a restarted server and got the same prompt count, reply and reasoning. A job that reads a conversation's next turn ahead reads up to the limit less one, so past seven eighths it reads rows an uncapped next turn will cut away; it still serves a capped one, and is left. A front end that sends the context size as `max_tokens` is refused on every request, as before; that is a question of its own.
- **Gates:** run and read by the gate runner at the landing head, with its hosted run.
- **Reviewed:** the design by the stand-in gating reviewer, who asked for the one owner and found the hole; its verdict on the code at the landing head is a condition of landing.

## A generating request is paced beside a prompt by default (2026-10-12, branch feat/auto-pacing, lands by fast-forward)

- **Goal:** the owner's decision of 2026-10-11: serving a request that is already generating while a prompt is read becomes an automatic, best-effort policy, on by default where pacing is possible, with an off switch and no number for a user to choose.
- **Done:** on one device or one tensor group with the whole model on it, `serve` paces by the automatic rule unless `--no-pacing` is given. `--generating-share` above 0 remains as the control: it replaces the rule by the fixed share of 2026-10-09, which is what production runs at 0.33 as this lands. The rule aims at a service of generated rows every 100 ms (`kServiceGapMs`, a time: ten tokens a second a reply) at the piece boundary nearest that gap, and a floor keeps prompts at half of the accounted time when services are slow (`PromptFloor`, `kPromptFloor`). A service is whole: the drafts' chain, the marks and the pass that verifies them are admitted once by the stage at a piece boundary with nothing owed, and the pass is recorded there with no second test (`serve_generated`, `Recorder::granted`). The rule acts only while a reply and a prompt both wait; otherwise every pass is formed and recorded as without pacing, and generated rows ride a prompt's pass that takes no longer than the gap. `infer::unpaced` in `model/place.hpp` is the one owner of where a stage is fed in pieces, read by the fit, the CLI and the start line `server: pacing: ...`; `/v1/health` gives the mode, the target and four counters. Design in docs/SERVER.md, A generating request beside a prompt.
- **The owner's decision on the default, 2026-10-12:** where the writing user and the waiting prompt differ, the automatic default favours replies, so the floor stays at one half. The fixed third's row stands beside the rule's in each table below; the floor is the one constant to revisit if prompts prove too slow.
- **Departures from the first design, each stated:** a service is due at the boundary nearest the target (elapsed plus half a piece), not once the target has passed, since otherwise every gap is above the target by construction; and the fixed share's probe after eight ridden passes is not taken under the rule, which has no price to measure again.
- **Tests:** the failing cases first: the suite's `cli` and `server` components fail on main (no switch, no `pacing` group in health) and pass on the change. The rule's account, clock, holds and predicates by hand in `server-passes`; in `server-passes-cpu` the scheduler on one device and on a tensor group, with the submitting-thread witness for main's dispatch where nothing overlaps, a drafted service forced through debt (every chain on the stage's grant with nothing owed, the charge whole, an unused grant, refused drafts, a failing draft, a client leaving), and a prompt read one token a pass ridden where fast and fed in pieces where slow; the fit's rows in `placement`; a missing backend left to the fit in `model-validation`. Planted faults fail them: a piece held ahead on one device (23 of 24 submissions behind) and on the group (every wait left a sum ahead), the gate off (10 of 10 chains without a grant), a pass's charge omitted, the whole-pass timer off.
- **Found on the way and corrected:** the suite's `server` component failed on Windows with the Radeon VII at an earlier head: beside a prompt read in slices under 64 rows the reply was served ten times a second where main gives it a token a pass, the ride decision resting on a row time such slices never measure. Slices that small now ride until a pass of theirs fed whole has taken longer than the gap, a ridden pass is fed whole, and every whole pass with prompt rows is timed as it retires.
- **Measured:** on the test machine, MI50s, every llmx server with `--host-cache-bytes` of 1 GiB, each binary built there from a detached tree: main 0.1.0+g7d15a2f07ef5 and the candidate 0.1.0+g8190676a0788; the fixed third and `--no-pacing` are the candidate's binary with the flag; the reference image is `mxxm/mx-llama.cpp:gfx906`. Two streams ran at once on disjoint cards and cores, each comparing only within its own; every cell completed with status 0, none waited for memory, and a compute job that is not this project's was alive in at most one monitor sample of a cell.
  The landing head is 8190676a0 with two later corrections and documentation. The rows below are measurements of 8190676a0. The later corrections act where a pass is ridden, where a prompt slice has fewer than 64 rows, and where a prompt-only pass forms in an overlap with no ready decoder, which was fed in pieces before and is fed whole after; the counters show no ridden pass and no small slice, nothing recorded shows whether the third case occurred, so the rows carry that limit and were not rerun at the landing source. ## A pass taken at a stage's last piece boundary reaches the share's account (2026-10-11, branch fix/final-piece-observed, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found by XDEV, reading main 32743460f:** with `--generating-share` above 0, a pass of generated rows recorded between two pieces of a prompt's stage is timed when the next piece waits for it. Taken at the stage's last boundary, no piece follows: the pass ran and retired, but its time never reached `StageShare`, so its charge, its price sample and the reset of the pieces since were lost. An omission in the account, not a wrong byte; its effect on the delivered share was not measured.
- **Done:** `Model::record_pass_stage`, which owns the pending ticket, settles it once the stage is submitted, and where the stage's own recording fails, with no wait where nothing is pending.
- **The failing test first:** `placement`: on one device and on a group of two that say they are no CPU, the paced pass with and without logits, a pass taken at the last boundary must be observed once and leave nothing pending, with an interior boundary as the control for a double observation; on main the last boundary's is never observed. The observation must follow the wait for the pass's ticket, and where the stage's next submission fails after a pass was taken it is still observed once and the error escapes; removing the settle, its wait, or its call on the failure path each fails the case. A pass apart whose own recording fails is given no ticket by the scheduler, as before.
- **Gates:** on the test machine, each read from its own exit status. At the landing head: a Vulkan build of every target without a warning, CTest 47 of 47 with one MI50, `placement` holding the three witnesses, and the suite's `docs` and `dead-code` components. Kept from d87f4df1d, whose `src/` is the landing head's byte for byte, only the test's two added witnesses, the documentation and this record differing: the suite on the CPU and on one MI50, every component passing, `baseline` skipping in both with no fixture model in that container, as the server's real-model pass and the numpy half of `raw-blocks` do, and Qwen3-8B Q8_0 through `tools/server_mix_check.py --ids` at `--generating-share 0.5` giving main's ids on one MI50 and on a tensor group of two. Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 `generate` of 64 greedy tokens and `logits` give main's bytes on the CPU and on one MI50, every command exiting 0. Timing, Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on one MI50, logical CPUs 4-7 and 12-15, main and the fix both with `--generating-share 0.33`, a reply beside a 29957-token prompt, in the order main, fix, fix, main: the reply's rate while the prompt is read 22.12 and 22.01 tok/s on main against 21.85 and 21.80 with the fix, 1.1 percent lower, the prompt read in 135.5 and 135.8 s against 135.4 and 135.3 s, pass gaps p99 73 and 73 ms against 75 and 74 ms, passes apart 5379 and 5350 against 5327 and 5332. The loss is consistent with the charge the fix restores, a pass at each stage's last boundary now paid for, but two runs an arm on a shared machine do not separate it from timing, code layout and contention. The machine was shared throughout: another measurement of the developer's on two other cards and the other eight logical CPUs, others' builds and tests, and a one-minute disk read probe on logical CPUs 12-15 as the first main run ended and the first fix run began; that round's monitor kept only the load average, 6 to 19, and container names, so what each run met on the CPUs, the disks and the cards is not known. The default path, which gives no pace, `bench --model` pp512/tg128 in the same order, twice, the second round with each command's own exit status, 0, and a monitor of processes, disks and cards at a load average of 15 to 16: pp512 837.7, 837.4, 843.8 and 839.6 on main against 836.9, 838.3, 840.7 and 840.5 tok/s, level; tg128 75.8, 76.3, 76.3 and 76.7 against 75.6, 75.9, 76.1 and 75.5, 0.7 percent lower in the mean with the ranges overlapping. The hosted run is the landing commit's.
- **Reviewed:** by XDEV, who found the defect, asked for the completion-order and failure-path witnesses and for the fixed share's documentation to promise no fraction, accepted the source, the tests and the documentation, and read the d87f4df1d logs itself; the timing, the identity and the landing head's checks were read by the developer from their files and given to XDEV before landing.

## The start line says up to how long a history requests still take turns (2026-10-11, branch fix/turns-start-line, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found on production:** the start line said uncapped requests filling the pool do not take turns, with the host tier at 10844 MiB against 17664 MiB for the longest history. O5REV read the code (devlog, 2026-10-11 04:47 UTC) and it is so: `Scheduler::yields` asks whether the yielding request's own history, `host_bytes(its length)`, fits the tier, and only a tier of 0 turns them off, so shorter histories do take turns.
- **Found again by XDEV's review (devlog, 2026-10-11 10:06):** on a model that keeps a state with no checkpoint slot `Scheduler::yields` refuses every turn (`checkpoints_free()` is 0), so the line must say that before any length; `turns_line` does, and the cases cover a partial tier with and without a state and a slot.
- **Done:** a tier that holds some histories and not the longest prints the longest history, in whole blocks, that still takes turns, with both sizes (`turn_tokens`, `short_tier_line` in `policy.hpp`, used by `no_turns`); a tier of 0 or one below a history keeps the present sentence. `docs/SERVER.md`, `docs/OPERATING.md` and AGENTS.md say it. One comment above `Scheduler::yields` gets its indentation.
- **Test:** `server-passes` by hand, the number and the line (the first commit fails on the old wording); the suite's `server` keeps the tier of 0 and the tier that holds a history, and adds a tier of 1 MiB on the 512-token model with a 128-token pool, whose one block takes a 64 MiB slab. A tier that holds part cannot be built on the synthetic models, whose copies are one slab each (`kHostSlab`, `Model::host_bytes`: CPU copies are rounded to 64 MiB like any other), so that half is held by hand in `server-passes`; a first attempt at 1 MiB on the 16-token model was silent because its context holds no whole block of the CPU's 128 and `no_turns` then asks `host_bytes(0)`.
- **Gates, at d02dbeb8d (a docs-only delta from the landing head), test machine, Linux container on CPUs 12-15, no card, each from its own exit status:** the test commit built alone, build exit 0, `llmx-server-passes-test` exit 1 on the partial-tier case; main 176f3748a and the head built, exit 0, the head with 0 warnings (numerics 83f52235e70612bb, equal to main's); CTest exit 0, 42 of 42; Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 ids and logits of main against the head on the CPU, `cmp` exit 0 (14 lines); the whole CPU suite exit 0, 27 components PASS and the skips for want of a model, numpy or a device (baseline family, raw-blocks' numpy form, the server's real-model pass). Not run: the MI50 server component and the identity on a card, the change touching no pass, kernel or fit (XDEV may ask). ## Timing-shaped test cases act from the scheduler's thread (2026-10-11, branch test/timing-margins, tests only, lands by fast-forward)

- **Why:** O5REV's audit of 2026-10-09 listed cases whose test thread sees a state of the scheduler and then acts, so a late thread fails them red or lets them pass without holding their point; `resumed_by_fork` failed on macOS with that shape.
- **Made deterministic, all through `Scheduler::on_retire` as `reprefilled` and `cancelled_short_donor` do:** `resumed_by_fork` (the second request submitted at the first's 50th sampled pass; the STATUS sentence calling it held without a clock is corrected), `cancel_while_paused_donor` (the cancel at the first pass retired after the pause, the submits before `run()`), `stall_holds_room` (F submitted at the first pass that finds the stall), `cancelled_while_paused` and the hybrid model's copy (cancelled at the first pass after a pause, and each must now end "cancel", where "length" was accepted), `disk_read_waits` (the follow-up's passes counted when the later request's last token is sampled, none, in place of `other_ms < 1500`), `disk_read_bound` (the read seen still in flight with no entry read at the follow-up's last sampled pass, in place of `ms < 1900`).
- **Left as clocks, and why:** `disk_age` (an age limit of five seconds is a wall clock by definition; the test thread reads the files after six turns, and a clock seam would be needed), `recorder_rule`'s 300 ms hold (no count in `Scheduler::Stats` says the scheduler waits in `quiet()`), `disk_cap_base`'s four-second sleep (a count of writes refused for the cap would hold it); each needs a product-side seam and none is added. `disk_never_blocks` and `job_forks_running` stay as audited. The two disk-read cases still depend on the read hold of two seconds, a test option, outlasting the scheduler thread's own work, with wide margins.
- **Each case still fails for its reason:** the fault each guards was planted in a copy of the scheduler and the case failed: admission going on during a stall (`if (!stalled || true)`) fails `stall_holds_room` with "started before the capped request holding its room ended"; promotion from host memory switched off fails `resumed_by_fork` with "0 promotions from host memory and 11264 tokens recomputed". The other cases were not planted.

## One line of what waits: a request arriving while two take turns (2026-10-10, branch feat/waiting-line, the second of a stack of two on feat/pool-edge, lands by fast-forward directly after it)

- **Why:** nothing left the queue while a request was paused. With turns at the pool's edge one of the two edge requests is always paused, so a request that arrived meanwhile, however small, waited for the older one's end, which turns make later: on the reproduction its first token came after 42.6 and 43.7 s on main and after 115.2 and 115.3 s on feat/pool-edge alone.
- **Done:** everything that waits stands in one line (`admit_waiting`, `Request::line_`). The requests paused for another's growth come first, oldest first, as before; then those that gave the pool's edge up and the queued ones, merged by the number each took when it began to wait, a yielder at its yield and a queued request at its submission. Admission walks the line and stops at the first that does not fit. Without turns the order is what it was.
- **The bound on both sides:** a queued request is behind only what waited before it, so it is admitted at the next change of turn if it fits beside the request that takes the edge; a request that arrives after a paused one began to wait stands behind it, and admission stopping at the first that does not fit keeps it there, so no stream of arrivals passes a paused request.
- **Measured, the reproduction (Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0, a tensor group of two MI50s, pool 16384), each cell run twice, a 64-token request sent 100 s after the second uncapped one:**

  | | main a1b8211b4 | feat/pool-edge alone | the stack before its rebase | the stack at 4fd5eebaf, one run |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | the arriving request's first token after | 42.6, 43.7 s | 115.2, 115.3 s | 3.2, 4.7 s | 6.0 s |
  | the newer edge request's longest wait | 87.0, 88.1 s | 11.7, 14.4 s | 14.4, 15.1 s | 13.7 s |
  | the older edge request's longest wait | 2.1, 2.1 s | 9.5, 9.4 s | 9.0, 10.6 s | 10.7 s |
  | tokens recomputed | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
  | the kept conversation's third turn, host tier 7262 MiB | not run | not run | not run | 768 reused (0 at 872b174c2, before the fix of the first record's fourth defect) |

- **The condition the review set before it was built is met in its first half and not to the letter in its second.** The arriving request waits less than a turn, 3 to 5 s where it waited 43 on main. The edge requests' longest waits were to stay within what feat/pool-edge alone gives, 11.7 and 9.5 s: the newer one's is 14.4 and 15.1 s against 11.7 and 14.4, the older one's 9.0 and 10.6 s against 9.5 and 9.4. The excess, about a second in one run of two each, is of the size of the arriving request's own three seconds of decoding inside a turn; that is a reading, not a measurement, and two runs a cell do not separate it from run-to-run spread.
- **Tests:** `server-resume`: a capped request submitted from the scheduler's thread once two uncapped requests have changed turns twice must be in a pass within two changes of turn and before either has ended (the failing commit; on feat/pool-edge it is first in a pass at pass 3267, after both had ended at 3139 and 3266; here at pass 1861, one change of turn on). `server-passes`: the simulated schedules walk one line, and a queued request is never admitted before a paused one that began to wait before it, nor a yielder before a queued one submitted before its yield.
- **After the rebase and the fix the arriving request waits 5.5 s at the rebased head and 6.0 s with the fix, still under a turn, and the edge requests' longest waits are 13.7 s and 10.6 to 10.7 s:** the newer one's within the first branch's range, the older one's about a second over it, as before the rebase. The other columns are the two runs each of the earlier heads.
- **Gates, at the code of this record's commit:** on the test machine Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 the same ids and logits as main 069dfaaa8 on the CPU and on one MI50, the suite's `server` and `qwen35` on the MI50, a CPU build without warnings, CTest 42 of 42, the CPU suite, the linked check as the list, `server-resume` under ThreadSanitizer in 846 s with no report; on Windows a build without errors, CTest 43 of 43 and the suite's `server`, `docs`, `dead-code`, `arch-boundary`; a hosted run at the stack's head named in the landing's devlog entry.
- **Reviewed:** F2DEV the design of the rule on 2026-10-08; O5REV the code at be66456de and 39670f4f6, the rebase at 872b174c2 and the fix at 4fd5eebaf.
- **What it does not reach:** a server that takes no turns, for want of host memory, still holds a queued request until the older edge request ends, as main does; its start line says so.

## Turns at the pool's edge, and the pool's fill in health (2026-10-09, branch feat/pool-edge, the first of a stack of two with feat/waiting-line and not to land without it, lands by fast-forward)

- **Why:** two uncapped requests larger together than the pool. The older one's growth paused the newer, which then had no token until the older ended: 87 s in the reproduction (Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0, a tensor group of two MI50s, pool 16384), and on a 200k pool as long as the older one takes to reach the limit.
- **Done:** uncapped requests that cannot all hold their room take it in turn (docs/SERVER.md, turns at the pool's edge). A running request whose growth step falls due after it has held the edge a turn, while an uncapped request is paused that would then fit, is paused in its place, its history kept whole, and goes to the back of the line of the paused (`Growth::turn`, `Growth::yields`, `Scheduler::yields`, `Request::line_`). A turn is the growth steps that make a change of turn a tenth of it. The change is timed from the yield to the first retired pass that carries the request the turn went to, held by its first admission's number, and the smaller of the last two timed counts (`Growth::change`), so one slow change, the first, which allocates the tier's slabs, does not lengthen the next turn. It applies only where the yielder's history can be kept: a host tier with room for it and, on a model that keeps a state, a free checkpoint slot.
- **The share is a constant.** `Growth::kTurnShare` is ten percent, picked from the measurement and written beside the constant with its reason, as the owner's rule of 2026-10-10 asks of a number nobody should have to choose: at 5, 10 and 20 percent a turn at histories of 14k tokens together is 14 to 20 s, 8 to 10 s and 8 s (one step), so 5 percent doubles the wait and 20 percent changes nothing at that size; at 200k, scaled by bytes and not measured, 200, 100 and 50 s. It is not a flag.
- **Also in it:** the pool's fill in `/v1/health`, `server.kv_tokens`, `requests.now.kv_tokens` and `reuse.device.now.kv_tokens`, the running requests' and the kept conversations' parts taken a pool and then the largest, and `pressure.since_start.turns`; and a line under the serving line for a server where turns were possible or asked for and will not happen, with the size that would hold a history (`no_turns`), silent where a tier holds one and on a CPU server at its default.
- **Defects of the rule itself, found on the way and fixed in it.** (1) A paused request's last history was refused by the host tier, which ranked it as a conversation that never came back, and 384 tokens were recomputed at its resume (`server-spec`, on the test machine's CTest); a paused request's own donor now ranks as one that came back. (2) Found by the review: each turn left a new copy in host memory and the copy before it stayed, outranking other users' kept conversations. A request's history made a donor, at a pause or at its end, now supersedes the copy its last pause left (`Request::paused_as_`, in `park`). Where a finished request's donor on a model that keeps a state ends at its prompt's checkpoint, it is shorter than the pause copy it supersedes; nothing is lost, the copy's rows past the prompt being decode rows, which a later turn's prompt does not fork. (3) Found by the review: the request a turn went to was held by its address and cleared only by a pass that carried it, so a receiver whose client left during the change left it set, a later request at that address would have matched it, and the rule would have stopped yielding until a restart. It is held by its first admission's number, which no later request carries; left unmet, it is overwritten by the next yield. (4) Found by my own reproduction at the rebased head, with a host tier of 7262 MiB where earlier runs had 10 to 13 GB: fix (2) held for one of the two requests only. A request that resumes by forking a copy promoted from host memory leaves the promoted donor on the devices where its room is not needed, the shorter request's case; evicted again, that donor stood for the stale host copy and cleared its superseded mark, so the shorter request's old copies piled up, about half a gigabyte each, and a kept conversation's copy was released from host memory for them, which a tier of 10 to 13 GB held without releasing and one of 7262 MiB did not, so the earlier runs passed. The donor promoted from a superseded copy is now superseded with it. A traced run showed it; `server-resume` holds it with a long and a short request, where the kept conversation's third turn reused 0 tokens before and its 256 after.
- **Measured, the reproduction, main a1b8211b4 against the branch before its rebase onto d99439620, each cell run twice:**

  | | main | branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | the newer request's longest wait for a token | 87.0, 88.1 s | 11.7, 14.4 s |
  | the older request's longest wait | 2.1, 2.1 s | 9.5, 9.4 s |
  | pauses, of them turns given up | 1, 0 | 21 to 23, 20 to 22 |
  | tokens recomputed | 0 | 0 |
  | a 64-token request sent during the turns, first token after | 42.6, 43.7 s | 115.2, 115.3 s |

  A change of turn there is 0.7 to 1.0 s and a step 8 s, so a turn is one step. The older request pays for the newer one's turns: in the first run it ended after 227 s against 154 s.
- **The last row is why this branch does not land alone.** Nothing leaves the queue while a request is paused, on main as here, and with turns one edge request is always paused, so a small request waits for the older one's end, which turns make later. That is a slowdown on a path main has; feat/waiting-line, on top of this, removes it (3.2 and 4.7 s at the stack's head), and the two land by consecutive fast-forwards with nothing between.
- **The newer request's rate reads higher here, 34.3 and 34.1 tok/s against 30.7 and 31.0, and is not explained.** It is tokens over the time from first token to end, pauses included, so it is the newer request ending 49 s sooner. It is not the drafter: drafts kept over the whole run are 12135 on main and 12168 here. A guess with one line behind it: the two decode in the same passes for about a minute on main and almost never here, and a request decoding beside another on this group read 6.0 tok/s against 21.6 nearly alone. Not measured apart.
- **A kept conversation beside the turns, same cards, twice:** a conversation of two turns kept before the two start (768 tokens, 200.6 MiB in host memory); after 20 changes of turn had filled the tier, 14 and 15 entries, 9.73 and 10.74 GB, its third turn reused 768 of 812 prompt tokens, promoted from host memory with no read from disk. The head before fix (2) was not run on the cards; that contrast is `server-resume`'s case on the dense model, 0 tokens reused before and 256 after. At the rebased head with the fix, one run on the cards with the host tier fixed at 7262 MiB: the conversation's third turn reused 768 of 812 tokens where the head before fix (4) reused 0, read back from disk and not used, and 6 entries (6.44 GB) stood in host memory after 20 changes of turn where 11 (7.31 GB) did.
- **Tests:** `server-resume`: two uncapped requests at the pool's edge, the newer decoding again before the older has ended, on the dense and the hybrid model (the failing commit; on main the newer waits from pass 729 to pass 2008, after the older one's last); a conversation of two turns surviving four changes of turn at least beside it, with a turn fixed at one step (`Scheduler::turn_steps`, a seam for tests beside `on_retire`); a request waiting for a turn cancelled while paused, passed over, a later pair still taking turns. No case reaches a receiver that leaves between a yield and its first pass: a round has no point between the two at which a test can act, and what holds that fix is that no address is kept. `server-passes`: `turn`, `change` and `yields` by hand, and turns in the simulated schedules, the yielder last in the line and the request the turn went to first among the uncapped paused. `server-spec`'s resumed-by-fork case counts one pause and one promotion at least, the two now taking turns, and still no token recomputed. The suite's `server`: the start line with no host memory given, and none with a tier that holds a history or on the CPU at its default.
- **`park` now reorders the host tier's entries.** Its three callers, the pause, a request's end and a job's parking, were read: none lies between an index into `host_` being taken and used, by reading the call sites a search gives, not every path.
- **Comments and the files' sizes:** main swept the server tier's files while this stack waited, so the stack adds no wall to them; `tests/server_spec.cpp`, the one file it touches that still held walls, is swept in a comment-only commit under it, its code proved unchanged with comments stripped. scheduler.hpp is 2919 lines on main and 2929 here, by the coordinator's decision of 2026-10-09 that the file grows by what the stack needs until its move-only split. Moves without a change, each to its owner: `add`, `sub`, `RowClass` with `class_at` and `clip`, and `draft_marks` to policy.hpp, with `less` new beside `sub`; `default_host_cache` to api.hpp beside the configuration it defaults.
- **Not measured together:** turns at the pool's edge and a share for generating requests (`--generating-share`); no case runs both, the share being 0 by default.
- **Reviewed:** F2DEV the design of the rule on 2026-10-08; O5REV the code at be66456de and 39670f4f6, the rebase at 872b174c2 and the fix at 4fd5eebaf.
- **Gotchas:** a save into host memory that throws leaves the yielder to recompute, as any pause does. A server without a host tier takes no turns and behaves as before. A superseded copy stays in host memory until its room is needed, so `reuse.host.now.entries` and `bytes` rise to the tier's size under turns and do not by themselves show a conversation pushed out.

## A generating request keeps a share of a device beside a prompt (2026-10-09, branches refactor/stage-recorders-pp and feat/paced-pieces, lands by fast-forward as two commits)

- **Found on production:** a chat that was writing its reply stood still while another conversation's long prompt was read. A generating request's row rode the pass that read the prompt and waited for that pass on every device. Measured on main before any change: Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 on a tensor group of two MI50s with the embedded drafter, one request generating beside a 49896-token prompt, 2.2 events a second with 1.8 s between passes that carry its tokens (57 to 65 alone); Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on one MI50 beside a 30000-token prompt, 0.72 tok/s with pauses of 2.4 s (73 alone).
- **Done:** `serve --generating-share X`, 0 up to 0.9, default 0, where nothing changes. Above 0, on one device or one tensor group, a prompt's pass is fed to its stage in pieces by the stage's thread, a piece ending at each part on a single device and at each sum on a group; the generating requests' rows go in passes of their own kind, in a second arena on every device, and are recorded between two pieces when their share is due. The share is an account of time owed on each stage (`StageShare` in the policy core). A layer split and a placement with a stage on the CPU refuse the flag by name as the server starts (`server::check_share`).
- **Step 1, its own commit, the base:** each device stage of a pipelined layer split past the first has a recorder, used only while another pass is in flight (`recorded_apart`); the first stage stays on the scheduler's thread. A first build that gave every device stage a recorder lost 3 to 8 percent, and an event log named the hand-over: the recorders' wakes cost 0.01 ms a pass, and the loss was the first stage's end published while the scheduler's thread sat in the retiring pass's logits wait and its sampling, so the last stage's submission came 1.1 ms a pass late. A thread costs a stage nothing by its wake and everything by where the scheduler's thread is when the stage ends. With the first stage inline the round is level with main (Qwen3-8B Q8_0 over two MI50s, `--dtype int8 --host-cache-bytes 0`, closed, two rounds, 128 tokens a reply; main, branch, branch, main in one session, at 4983b938f against main 8278c6b7f):

  | prompts | users | main tok/s (first, last) | branch tok/s (two arms) | inter-token p50 / p99, main | branch |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 128 | 1 | 70.9, 70.1 | 69.6, 70.0 | 13.3 / 14 ms | 13.4 to 13.5 / 14 to 15 |

On that model the tool's CLI comparison fails for its first request at every arm, main with and without the drafter included, whose ids are the head's: a difference between `generate` and the server on main, reported in the devlog and not this change's.
- **Radeon VII, Windows, the proprietary driver, at c28038b3c:** a fresh Vulkan build, CTest 48 of 48; the same tool on Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 at share 0 and one half, each matching the CLI, one file (500674 bytes); a request generating beside a 29957-token prompt, two runs: 1.17 and 1.20 tok/s with 0.87 s between tokens at share 0, 39.2 and 39.2 tok/s with nothing over 0.07 s at one third, the read 55.8 and 55.7 s against 74.5 and 74.4 s.
- **What a layer split would pay, and why it is refused:** fed in pieces, a prompt's pass stays in flight for its stage's device time and a sequence is in one pass at a time, so the stages stop overlapping on the prompt: Qwen3-8B Q8_0 over two MI50s read 30000 tokens in 120.1 s at one half against 46.0 s at share 0, one run, on an earlier head. The repair is a sequence in consecutive passes at consecutive stages (`docs/MULTI-DEVICE.md`, order of work, 4), a step of its own.
- **Reached by tests and by no product path until that step:** the scheduler gives a share to any placement that `Model::paces`, a pipelined layer split among them, and only `serve` refuses the split (`check_share`). So `Model::stage_ready` past its first stage, `Backend::done` with its Vulkan override, and a pass apart at each stage of a split are the layer-split step's, kept here with their tests (`server-passes-cpu`, `server-resume`) for it.
- **Four faults on the way, each found by measurement and held by a hand check in `server-passes`:** (1) the share as a fading average of each side's time delivered 58 percent at a setting of one half and 35 at one quarter; it is an account of time owed. (2) A ride priced by the line fitted to the passes' retirement times, which under a share include the wait until the rows are due, sent generated rows riding the prompt's last slices, a gap of 0.5 to 0.8 s at the end of every read at one quarter and one third; a ride is priced by what a stage's thread measures. (3) Priced by the last pass measured, one pass of over half a second under a neighbour's load held the price and the rows rode for two minutes; the price is the least of the last eight, and a ride goes apart for one pass after eight prompt passes (`RideRun`). (4) A pass recorded behind a piece held ahead is not measured, and charged the last pass measured it kept itself rare and unmeasured after one slow pass; every charge uses the price, a pass spends no more than two at the price, and no piece is held ahead while a pass apart waits.
- **Tests:** `server-passes` by hand (`rides`, `RideRun`, `StageShare`, the two kinds in `round_steps`) and its simulated executor with two kinds of pass; `server-passes-cpu` over backends that say they are no CPU at one half and one quarter, over stages of groups at one half, and a request cancelled, a submission failing and a stop from inside a piece; `server-resume`'s recorder rule fed in pieces; `backend-vulkan`, two sequences of sums interleaved on one collective; `tests/cli.py`, the refusal on the CPU.
- **Gates:** the tables above, each binary's version line its commit, llmx alone on its cards at default clocks, logical CPUs 0-3 and 8-11; the many-user arms at c28038b3c against main d85a59616. Rebased over the tensor-split fixes and the comment sweep at 3e28c8a11, production's cell reads the same (2.27 and 2.28 events a second at share 0, 20.64 and 20.70 at one quarter, 26.24 and 26.29 at one third, 38.03 and 37.76 at one half; reads of 180, 237, 264 and 350 s), with one gap of 1.26 s in one run at one half as another agent's 27B server loaded on other cards. At that head on the test machine: a Vulkan build of every target without a warning, CTest 47 of 47 with one MI50, `backend-vulkan` and `vulkan-lifetime` on two, the suite on the CPU and on one MI50, `server-passes-cpu` and `http` under the thread sanitizer with no report, the recorder rule's three cases ten of ten unplanted and none of ten with a device call made outside the hold, and the many-user ids main's on one MI50, a group of two and a layer split; on the Radeon VII CTest 48 of 48 and one ids file at share 0 and one half. The hosted run is named in the landing's devlog entry.
- **Reviewed:** step 1 as the base and the pieces' design on a tensor group by F2DEV, whose two points are in (the collective's invariant where its parity flips, the interleaved sums in `backend-vulkan`); the price and the ride on 2026-10-09 and the whole stack at d0c48f569 by O5REV, no finding that held the code, whose four points are in (the refusal naming its cause, the names the next step owns, this line, the two comments).
## A two-shot sum's shares begin on the device's offset alignment (2026-10-09, branch fix/two-shot-offsets, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found by XDEV's review of main a1b8211b4, by arithmetic:** a sum over three or more members that takes two shots binds each member's share of the rows at the share's own float offset. Equal shares of 327680 floats over three members begin at floats 0, 109227 and 218454, bytes 12 and 8 past a 16-byte boundary, and a device may require a storage-buffer offset to be a multiple of 16 bytes (`minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment`). No failure on an MI50 is claimed; a device with that limit would be given offsets it does not take.
- **Done, a fix and not a refusal:** the shares are the equal ones rounded up to the largest offset alignment of the members' devices, in floats, and the gather rows are sized for that. Which float falls in which share changes no sum, each float being the same members' in the same order, and where the alignment is four bytes the shares are the equal ones as before. The offset of the residual a caller hands a sum stays the caller's, as for every operation.
- **The failing test first:** `vulkan-buffer`, which needs no device: the shares over 3, 4 and 5 members at alignments of 1, 4, 16 and 64 floats must cover the floats once, in order, each that holds a float beginning on the alignment; with it the share arithmetic moved, unchanged, to a function the test reads, and 32 of its cases failed.
- **Gates, for the four fixes and the comment-only commit under them, which land as one fast-forward:** on the test machine at the stack rebased on main d99439620, fresh builds whose version lines are their commits: a Vulkan build of every target without a warning; CTest 47 of 47 with one MI50; `backend-vulkan` and `vulkan-lifetime` on three MI50s, the collective of three with its two-shot sums, the cards reporting an offset alignment of 4 bytes, so their shares are the equal ones; the suite on the CPU and on one MI50, every component passing but `raw-blocks`, which needs numpy the machine's image lacks and runs in the hosted jobs, with `baseline` skipped there for want of its model and run by the hosted HF job; `tools/server_mix_check.py --logprobs` on Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on a group of two MI50s and on a layer split of two, each main's file byte for byte (502703 and 502992 bytes). `bench --model` on Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on the group of two, tg128 tok/s, main, head, head, main in three sessions: 92.64 and 93.65 against 91.81 and 92.28, 92.66 and 91.24 against 93.89 and 93.05, 92.50 and 94.24 against 94.00 and 92.95, pp512 between 1369.9 and 1372.2 in every arm; the head is inside main's two arms in two sessions and 0.4 percent under the lower in one, cause unassigned. On the Radeon VII under Windows a Vulkan build and CTest 48 of 48; the collective does not exist there, so the two-shot change does not run on it. The hosted run passed on the stack before these records took their gates (run 38016796406) and again at the head that lands.
- **Reviewed:** the four fixes and their tests by XDEV at 0a45101da, no defect; the rebase's delta, by range-diff, and the comment-only commit, by a stripper of its own, by O5REV.

## A context drops its views of the logits pages before the pages (2026-10-09, branch fix/logits-host-outlives, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found by XDEV's review of main a1b8211b4:** on a tensor group the logits rows are host pages that each member of the head's group imports. `ExecContext` declared the first member's view (`logits_buf`) before the pages (`logits_host`), so at the context's end the pages were freed while that view still lived, and a device keeps imported memory for as long as its buffer does. No device failure was observed; the order broke the import's contract on every such context.
- **Done:** the pages are declared before every buffer that wraps them, so the views go first. Where a grown context replaces them, the views were already replaced before the pages, and a context is assigned only over a fresh one (`reserve_passes`).
- **The failing test first:** `placement`: a context holding pages and two buffers that look, as they go, whether the pages are still mapped; on main the first member's view finds them gone.
- **Gates and review:** its own test on Windows, and the stack's gates and readers in the record of the two-shot sum's shares above.

## A shard whose write fails drains its backend before its storage goes (2026-10-09, branch fix/shard-write-drain, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found by XDEV's review of main a1b8211b4:** the loader's hook gives a tensor group's member its shard as storage of its own and writes the shard's zero runs, and in a mapped load its file runs, before it returns the buffer. A write that threw after an earlier one was queued unwound the hook's only reference, so the storage was freed with work pending on it; the model's own drain cannot cover it, since the model holds the buffer only once the hook has returned.
- **Done:** the hook drains the backend before the error leaves it (`planning_adopt` in `inference/load.hpp`).
- **The failing test first:** `model-validation`, on the asynchronous test backend: a shard whose second file run fails in a mapped load, and one whose second zero run fails in a streamed load, must give the error with nothing pending and nothing freed early; on main both free the storage with one write pending.
- **Gates and review:** its own test on Windows, and the stack's gates and readers in the record of the two-shot sum's shares above.

## A tensor group is fitted by its largest member (2026-10-09, branch fix/fit-every-member, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found by XDEV's review of main a1b8211b4:** the fit and the automatic KV budget asked `footprint` for a group without naming a member and got member 0's. Since covering blocks (the record of 2026-10-08) a group's members are uneven: with experts 768 wide in Q4_K at width 4 the outer members cover one block of 256 columns and the inner ones two, so a model could be accepted, and its KV sized, as if the inner members held half their expert bytes. XDEV's probe on the test's layout: 442368 bytes of layer weights on member 0 against 884736 on member 1, and a budget of 443392 accepted.
- **Done:** `footprint` with no member named gives each part as the largest any member's is (each tensor, cache, head slice and drafter part), which is what both fit calls in `place_model` take. Over-counting is possible where different members are largest in different tensors; the fit errs toward refusing.
- **The failing test first:** `shard`: the footprint a group is fitted by must hold of every tensor at least what each member does, and a budget short of the largest member's layer by what the smallest saves must be refused; on main it fails at member 1.
- **Gates and review:** its own test on Windows, and the stack's gates and readers in the record of the two-shot sum's shares above.
- **Unchanged:** a model whose shards are even, as a dense file's are, is fitted as before, since each part is then the same on every member.

## The hosted Linux CPU job's limit is 20 minutes (2026-10-09, branch ci/cpu-limit, the workflow and its page only, lands by fast-forward)

## The disk tier's identity covers every shard of a model (2026-10-09, branch fix/disk-identity-shards, on fix/disk-age-ancestors, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found by:** XDEV's review of main a1b8211b4, reproduced there with two three-shard models, and rechecked against the code before the fix: `DiskTier` took the digest of the one path the server was given, the first shard, and `Model::host_identity` names layouts, placements and types, no weights.
- **The defect:** a sharded model whose first shard holds metadata alone has the same first shard as any model of that metadata. Two such models with different tensors had one identity, so under `--disk-cache-keep` the second adopted the first one's entries and a request matching their tokens would have continued the other model's history.
- **Done:** the tier asks the reader for the model's files (`model_files`: the path given and every shard `read_gguf` finds tensors in) and the identity's model line is each one's digest in order. A shard of metadata alone after the first is not hashed: the reader refuses a set whose shards' metadata differ from the first's.
- **Entries already kept are not dropped.** A one-file model's identity text is byte for byte what it was, and the change is in `src/server` alone, outside the numerics fingerprint: this pair changes no fingerprinted file, so the fingerprint is main's own at the landing head, whatever that is, and a server updated to it adopts what the one before it left if its fingerprint holds. A sharded model's entries are dropped by the model line, as they must be.
- **A first form of this was withdrawn before review:** it had the reader record its files (`src/format/gguf.hpp`), which is among the fingerprinted sources, so it changed the fingerprint to `5cefa0dfd6241ca8` and would have dropped every kept entry for a change of no bit.
- **Test:** the suite's `server`: two models of three shards, the same first shard and different tensors, each served with a disk tier, must write different identities, each naming every file's digest. On main the two texts are the same. `server-resume`'s disk root holds a GGUF of no tensors where it held a text file, since the tier now reads the model's headers.
- **Comments:** the lines this touches in `disk_tier.hpp` are a sentence or two, the file having been swept by the fix below. `tests/server.py`, touched here, has its eight long blocks cut in the comment-only commit under the pair (token-identical), and `tests/server_resume.cpp` has none on main.
- **Gates, at the pair's top head on the test machine (CPU, four cores, no card):** a Linux CPU build with no warning, CTest 42 of 42 and the whole CPU suite with every component passing but the skips for want of a model, numpy or a device; `docs` and `dead-code` on a Windows CPU build; the hosted runs of both gate branches are named in the landing's devlog entry.
- **Reviewed:** by O5REV (the code at the heads it read on d99439620, the rebase by range-diff); found by XDEV's review of main a1b8211b4.
- **Left:** the list of a model's files belongs to the reader and moves to `src/format/gguf.hpp` with the sweep of the fingerprinted files.

## The age limit at a restart follows a conversation, not a file (2026-10-09, branch fix/disk-age-ancestors, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found by:** XDEV's review of main a1b8211b4, reproduced there on the store and the index, and rechecked against the code before the fix: `DiskStore::adopt_from` left out each file older than the limit by its own modification time, and a renewal touches only the file used (`DiskTier::renew`), the files below it kept young in the index's memory alone.
- **The defect:** a conversation picked up again an hour ago stands on files written when it began. While the server runs the index keeps them, since something beyond them was used. At a restart under `--disk-cache-keep` the store dropped the old ones by their own age, and the fresh ones, reached by nothing, were dropped after them: the conversation was read again whole.
- **Done:** the store adopts every file of its identity and says when each was last used; `DiskTier::adopt` enters them in the index and then applies the age limit there (`expire`), where a file goes only when nothing beyond it was used within the limit. The start line counts what the limit dropped. A conversation unused past the limit is still dropped at a restart, whole.
- **Entries already kept:** nothing is dropped by this change that was kept before, and files in `src/server` are outside the numerics fingerprint, so an update that carries only this adopts what the server before it left.
- **Comments:** `disk_tier.hpp` and `disk_store.hpp` are swept to the rule of a sentence or two, four blocks each, what they said in more being on docs/src/server.md already; the code is unchanged by it. `tests/server_resume.cpp` has no long block on main, and the gates and reader of this change are in the record of the identity change above.
- **Tests:** `server-resume`: a first turn's files made two days old and a second turn's left fresh, a restart under a limit of a day, the third turn forking the 512 tokens of the second; on main 0 of 2 files were adopted and nothing reused. `disk-store`: adoption takes a file whatever its age and gives its last use. The case of an old conversation dropped at a restart is unchanged and passes.

## A prompt that does not fit its context is refused with its numbers or cut at a turn's end (2026-10-08, branch feat/context-overflow, lands by fast-forward)

- **Why (the user, 2026-10-08):** a server at its context limit must stay usable; a conversation that outgrows the context got a 413 on every turn from then on. "Have an option to refuse and cut", with cheap markers for where to cut; the default stays `refuse`.
- **Done:** `serve --context-overflow refuse|shift`, one rule a value on all four generating routes. `refuse`, the default, answers 413 with the prompt's tokens, the limit and the flag's name. `shift` cuts the prompt before the scheduler sees it: a chat route drops the oldest messages after the system message, whole messages, a kept window starting at a user message so a tool call stays with its results, and renders the rest again; a text route keeps its leading block and drops whole turns after it, or whole steps of rows where the prompt has no end token. Every reply carries a `context` object beside `usage`: `tokens`, `limit`, and after a cut `dropped_messages`, `dropped_tokens` and `at_marker`.
- **The index** is one scan of the prompt's ids for the tokens the tokenizer's metadata marks as ends, a row offset a turn (`src/server/context_cut.hpp`, new, 74 lines, with no model, tokenizer or template in it); the chat routes fall back to rendering the conversation up to each message where the scan finds another number of ends than there are messages. `api.hpp` goes from 839 to 910 lines; `scheduler.hpp` is untouched.
- **Steps from the prompt's start, not a target from its end:** a cut drops to the first cut point one step, half the limit, past the leading block, or two steps, the fewest that fit. The first form, "drop until half is left", moved the cut at every turn, since every turn's conversation is a little longer, and so read the window again every turn; counted from the start the cut stays at the same message for a step's worth of conversation. On the real model's test, Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 on a pool of 2048 tokens, the cuts over fourteen turns are none for eight turns and then 10 messages on each of the six after, and each turn cut where the one before was reuses it.
- **What a cut costs, and what no marker saves:** the turn that cuts reads everything past the leading block again, on every model; a saved state holds the dropped messages, and without one the kept rows' positions change. At one half each new row of conversation costs about one row read again. On Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 at 262144 tokens that is a wait of up to about eight minutes at a cut, once every 131k tokens of conversation; reading the shifted window ahead while idle is the measured second step and is not built.
- **The failing test first:** the suite's `server` component: on main the server does not take the flag; with the change the synthetic chat model on a pool of 128 tokens refuses by default on the four routes with the numbers, and under `shift` a chat of six turns is cut by 0, 0, 4, 4, 6 and 8 messages, each reply and prompt those of the kept messages sent alone, a text prompt by one step after its first rows; the Q8_0 fixture on 2048 tokens as above, a pool that large so that the reuse is held on a device too, where a window under 449 tokens takes another tile split at every length. `context-cut` (new CTest) holds the cut alone.
- **Not built:** the idle read of a shifted window; a cut that could keep part of a turn.
- **Measured, gates:** on Windows CTest 43 of 43 and the whole CPU suite; the test machine's CPU gates, the suite's server component on an MI50, identity of Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 with main and the hosted run are named in the landing's devlog entry.
- **Reviewed:** by F2DEV, no finding in the code: the steps counted from the prompt's start taken as an improvement on the note, the estimate checked by the real render before anything is served; two notes taken, a clause on the fallback's cost in `message_ends` and a sentence of SERVER.

## A request drafts while another waits for room (2026-10-08, branch perf/draft-while-waiting, lands by fast-forward)

- **Found on production:** three requests generated 7156 tokens with at most 34 verifies between them. A pass took no draft while any request was queued or paused, a rule no record names a measurement for, so the request that held the pool ran at its plain rate for exactly as long as another waited for it to end.
- **Measured first** (two MI50s, Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 with its embedded drafter, production's flags and a 16384-token context, a chat generating to the pool's end with a second one paused beside it): from the pause to the first request's end, 160 s and about 3300 tokens, the verifies stood still at 253, and the request ran at 20.8 tok/s.
- **Done:** a request paused or queued for room no longer stops the drafts; it waits for the running requests to end or grow, which their drafts bring sooner, and a draft stays inside the drafting request's own reservation. The rule stays where every seat is taken and a request is queued for one, which is the half a measurement asked for (below). `scheduler.hpp` is 2769 lines before and 2771 after.
- **The same reproduction with the change:** the first request runs at 31.3 tok/s and ends after 147 s where it took 220 s, 1328 verifies by then; the second, which waits for it, has its whole reply 71 s sooner.
- **Why half of the rule stays:** removed whole, it cost output where requests queue for seats. Qwen3.8-27B Q8_0 with its embedded drafter, 16 seats, closed loops of 32 and 64 users of 128-token prompts and replies, tok/s of output, two rounds interleaved with main:

  | shape | users | main | the rule removed whole | the half kept |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | tensor group of two | 32 | 107.9, 106.2 and 106.0, 104.0 | 105.2, 106.3 | 105.4, 104.6 |
  | tensor group of two | 64 | 107.3, 107.3 and 107.5, 107.3 | 107.2, 107.5 | 107.7, 106.2 |
  | layer split of three | 32 | 136.8, 136.5 and 133.0, 136.2 | 122.4, 133.2 | 131.9, 130.3 |
  | layer split of three | 64 | 140.4, 140.4 and 136.9, 138.5 | 127.6, 134.4 | 139.0, 136.2 |

  Main was run in both sessions, so its cells hold four figures. On the split of three the whole removal lost 3 to 10 percent of the output and raised the first-token p99 from 48.4 to 51.0 and 54.6 s at 64 users, the passes feeding 488 and 987 drafts where main fed 130 and 165; with the half kept the cells are within main's own spread but for 32 users on the split, 131.9 and 130.3 against 133.0 to 136.8, which I leave stated and not explained. With 64 seats, where nothing queues, both builds are level (group 110.5, 123.9, 126.8 against 110.8, 125.4, 127.5 at 16, 32 and 64 users; split 132.9, 154.5, 155.5 against 135.6, 154.6, 155.7).
- **What the split's loss says and this branch does not fix:** drafts beside 16 decoders on a layer split of three cost output, and the price that should refuse them takes them. That is the price's defect, with the third draft it leaves on a group of two (the record of the drafting rounds); the kept half of the rule covers it only where requests queue for seats.
- **The failing test first:** `server-spec`: on two seats and 8 blocks a request with drafts beside a queued request the pool has no room for must feed the drafts it feeds alone, which on main it does not, feeding none of them; on one seat, with a second request queued for it, it feeds none.
- **Measured, gates:** the two tables above; on Windows CTest and the suite's server, qwen35, docs, dead-code and version components; the test machine's CPU gates with the linked check, identity of Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0 with main and the hosted run are named in the landing's devlog entry.
- **Reviewed:** by F2DEV, no finding: the rule narrowed to its measured half, its reason beside it; the price's taking drafts beside many decoders on a layer split named as its own defect and left as one item with the third draft on the group.
